title: Prior visual context accelerates the emergence of object representations
abstract: Our knowledge about how the world is structured allows for predictions about what objects we might see next. Visual context is known to impact the perception of subsequent objects, but we do not know what context does to the mental representation of those objects. Using MEG, we tested how a scene context changes the neural representation of visual objects, and whether the context simply enhances expected object representations, or if it acts to reorganise the temporal trajectory of object information in the brain. Using temporal generalisation decoding, we show that multiple dimensions of semantic information are shifted up to 200 ms earlier when the object and the prior context are congruent, and this temporally-shifted decoding was related to behavioural object recognition speed. This suggests that prior context can warp the temporal trajectory through which object representations are accessed and accelerate the emergence of semantic object representations in the mind.

title: Kilohertz electrical stimulation drives widespread neuronal activation and temporal interference imposes focal rhythmic modulation
abstract: Temporal interference (TI) stimulation has attracted attention as a non-invasive approach that can target deep brain structures through interacting kilohertz-frequency electric fields. Its basic premise is that TI stimulation evokes neuronal responses through low-frequency amplitude modulation (AM), while the underlying kilohertz-frequency stimulation is ineffective to induce activity, the latter of which has not been tested rigorously at the cellular level. Here, we combined two-photon imaging in mouse models with immunohistochemistry and computational modeling to characterize spatiotemporal patterns of neuronal responses during TI stimulation. We found that kilohertz-frequency stimulation was sufficient to evoke activity without AM. In contrast, AM organized neuronal activity into rhythmic responses at AM frequency, with the strongest entrainment near the center of interference. Thus, kilohertz-frequency stimulation can drive widespread neuronal activation, upon which TI imposes focal rhythmic modulation. Our results provide a framework for refining TI stimulation and highlight the potential of kilohertz-frequency stimulation for brain stimulation.

title: Understanding Performance Plateaus and Representation Collapse in 3D MRI Transformers Trained to Classify Brain Disease
abstract: In medical imaging AI, we commonly assume that diagnostic classifiers will increase in accuracy if they are trained on more data, but in reality, their performance often plateaus. To understand this behavior, we ran a spectral analysis of 3D vision transformers, a common supervised deep learning model that can be trained to classify disease based on 3D brain MRI. For simpler classification methods such as linear discriminant analysis, the classifier performance AUC(N), when trained on a sample of size N, is known to depend on the encoder's eigenspectrum. Each class-discriminative direction in the latent space contributes only after the sample size N reaches a threshold, so the spectrum influences how performance scales with training data. Building on this theory, we show that supervised transformers compress almost all of their discriminative signal into one principal component (EVR@1 = 0.90--0.96): after this representation collapse happens, no further directions cross the threshold as training data increases, and accuracy plateaus. In principle, this plateau in performance could be due to either the encoder's learned feature space or the difficulty of the task. To distinguish these cases, we trained three types of supervised 3D transformers (ViT3D, MINiT, NIT) and, as a non-collapsing alternative, a frozen self-supervised encoder (DINO), to classify people with dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI) versus cognitively normal (CN) individuals from 3D brain MRI, using data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). We froze each encoder and applied it to a new task, so that only the task difficulty varied. An easy task encoder (Dementia vs CN), transferred to the harder task (MCI vs CN), did not reproduce the plateau (MINiT threshold 9.2), but full retraining did (2758.5). The plateau is therefore due to the learned encoder, rather than task difficulty. Ranking the feature directions by the proportion of the disease signal they contain, we were able to identify a sign of representation collapse, i.e., a single dominant spike in the latent feature eigenspectrum. This spike was 11--26 times larger than predicted from the rest of the spectrum for the disease-trained (supervised) encoders, but was absent for DINO (0.66). To predict how transformer accuracy scales with the number of training scans, a large spike in the encoder spectrum suggests that the representation has collapsed and additional scans will not help; a small spike means that the signal is spread across many encoder latent space directions, and more training data should boost the classifier performance.

title: Striatal D2-neurons gate D1-mediated associative encoding under uncertainty
abstract: Goal-directed actions are established through the encoding of predictive relationships between behaviour and its consequences, a process involving dopamine-dependent plasticity in the dorsal striatum. Early phases of learning entail complex associative landscapes from which useful action-outcome contingencies must be identified. Although dopamine processes are central to associative learning, the cellular mechanisms through which behaviourally relevant plasticity is selected from competing signalling events remain unknown. Here we show that D2-spiny projection neurons (D2-SPNs) are transiently recruited during the earliest stages of instrumental learning, when critical action-outcome contingencies emerge. We identify a dominant cell-to-cell transmodulation process by which D2-SPNs regulate dopamine-dependent signalling by constraining protein kinase A activity in D1-SPNs. This mechanism overrides extracellular dopamine signals and can be reproduced in vivo through calibrated optogenetic activation of cAMP signalling. Enhancing D2[->]D1-SPN transmodulation during uncertain reinforcement schedules durably improves action-outcome encoding, revealing a mechanism through which striatal networks promote relevant contingencies under associative ambiguity.

title: Real-time noise cancellation for EEG monitoring and brain-computer interfaces
abstract: Raw electroencephalography (EEG) data suffer from a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Effective real-time cleaning of EEG would improve the robustness of EEG monitoring, brain-computer interfaces, and brain-state-dependent stimulation applications in both laboratory and real-life environments. Here, we present a real-time source-estimate-utilizing noise-discarding algorithm (rtSOUND) for EEG noise suppression. We adapted the established offline SOUND algorithm for real-time use and implemented it into an open-source EEG-processing software. Instead of using conventional temporal filtering, SOUND operates the data with a spatial filter. This makes it particularly suitable for real-time applications, since each streamed data sample can be cleaned separately in near real-time. Unlike temporal filtering methods, SOUND does not make assumptions about the frequency content of noise and brain signals but assumes that the noise topographies differ from those generated by brain activity. With an EEG forward model, rtSOUND cross-validates the EEG time series and estimates the spatial distribution of noise, resulting in a data-cleaning linear spatial filter. Each streamed EEG sample is processed synchronously, and the filter is periodically updated in an asynchronous parallel process. The algorithm rapidly updates the spatial filter in response to changes in the data, ensuring that noise reduction is both immediate and accurately adapted to the current EEG state. rtSOUND was validated with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS)-EEG and resting-state EEG datasets measured from 25 healthy subjects. SNR of both TMS-evoked potentials and resting-state data consistently improved across various metrics. rtSOUND particularly benefitted channels with poor SNR, while retaining the waveforms in high-quality channels. The algorithm was fast enough to process data streamed at 5 kHz. rtSOUND improves the SNR of EEG in real time, providing a robust method to improve signal quality for brain-state-monitoring applications.

title: Supramodal Coding of Detection and Confidence in the Human Cortex
abstract: Perception is inherently multisensory, yet it remains unclear whether the brain detects stimuli and evaluates confidence in these detections using circuits shared across senses or circuits specific to each modality. Prior evidence is limited: scalp electrophysiology cannot localize where a shared code operates, whereas functional imaging cannot resolve its timing. We recorded intracranial activity (stereoelectroencephalography) in eight patients with epilepsy who performed a near-threshold audiovisual detection task in which they reported, on each trial, whether a visual, auditory, or audiovisual stimulus was present and rated their confidence, both overall and separately for each modality. Analyzing high-gamma activity at the single-channel and region-of-interest levels, we found that stimulus detection involved a broadly distributed, largely supramodal set of cortical regions responding regardless of modality, including the insula, dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, and superior temporal gyrus. Multivariate decoders trained to distinguish detected from undetected stimuli in one modality generalized to the other modality, indicating a shared detection code within these regions. Confidence relied on a more mixed architecture but was also substantially supramodal. Finally, the auditory cortex encoded confidence information about its non-preferred (visual) modality, with a similar effect in the visual cortex for auditory confidence, suggesting that the involvement of sensory cortices in confidence is not confined to its preferred input.

abstract: Our understanding of cell division control traditionally comes via using liquid broths or 2D flat-plate cultures - which cannot recapitulate the complex visco-elasto-plastic properties of natural habitats such as tissues, mucus, and soil. Consequently, how such regimes of physical confinement influence proliferative growth remains poorly understood. Here, using engineered, mechanically tunable and transparent growth matrices, we directly visualize yeast budding and division across 3D viscoelastic regimes. We discover that elevated physical confinement drastically prolongs budding intervals without any physiological defects or activating global regulatory programs. Remarkably, extended cell division times are not associated with transcriptional or proteomic signatures of mechanosensation or cell cycle regulation. Rather, 3D confinement physically constrains the volumetric growth of incipient buds - manifesting as delayed cell cycle progression. Hence, our findings establish that physical constrainment regulates eukaryotic cell division.

abstract: Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.

abstract: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, allergic disease associated with refractory pain in patients, yet the function of the nervous system in EoE pathogenesis remains ill-defined. Here we elucidate a mouse neuroimmune circuit that is linked to type 2-associated allergic inflammation and clinical responses in the esophagus, including pain. In a mouse allergy model, allergen exposure evokes pain-like behavior, increases esophageal Nav1.8 + sensory innervation density, and alters nociceptor sensitization. Thoracic dorsal root ganglia (DRG) show expression of type 2 cytokine receptors Il4ra and Il13ra1 , and IL-4 and IL-13 sensitize DRG neurons to noxious agents. Mechanistically, conditional deletion of Il4ra in mouse NaV1.8 + neurons attenuate the above allergen-induced phenotypes as well as the levels of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1); in parallel, IGF-1 receptor inhibition also dampens these disease features. Finally, EoE patient samples show increased esophageal neuronal density when compared with controls. Our findings thus describe a type 2 neuroimmune circuit that potentially contributes to EoE pathogenesis, including pain.

abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. The system provides mechanical integrity, photothermal responsiveness and NIR-assisted local drug release. In a mouse TMJ-OA model, SFZICC MNs combined with NIR irradiation reduce mechanical hypersensitivity, anxiety-like behaviors, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascularization, and outperform free CCA, blank microneedles and drug-loaded microneedles without NIR. Mechanistically, CCA directly interacts with MMP3, MMP9 and MMP13 and moderately inhibits their catalytic activities in vitro, while reducing intracellular superoxide accumulation, NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and MMP protein abundance. In vivo imaging further supports reduced overall MMP-associated proteolytic activity. These findings support SFZICC MNs as a locally responsive therapeutic platform for TMJ-OA.

abstract: Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

abstract: A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations.

abstract: The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

abstract: Understanding how global change reshapes species distributions remains a central challenge in ecology, yet most global assessments treat environmental drivers as static, uniform, or aggregate influences. This obscures where, why, and how specific drivers generate ecological risk or opportunity. Here, we apply explainable machine learning to assess how climate averages, variability, extremes, and land cover are projected to reshape future distributions of 1,992 terrestrial mammals. Using Shapley Additive Explanations with species distribution models, we quantify the directional contribution of 16 environmental drivers and track how these contributions change over space and time. We propose two ecological diagnostics, directional turnovers and favorability shifts, that reveal where drivers switch from favorable to unfavorable, or the reverse, and where their influence strengthens or weakens without sign reversal. While not designed to infer causation, our framework assesses whether projected spatial patterns align with ecological expectations. We show that climate extremes impose intense but spatially restricted impacts, temperature-related drivers dominate exposure patterns, particularly for specialist species, and the same driver can impose risk in one region while creating opportunity in another. By decomposing projected biodiversity change into driver-specific signatures, our framework advances biodiversity forecasting toward a more actionable understanding of ecological risk and opportunity.

abstract: Three trematode parasites, Schistosoma haematobium , Opisthorchis viverrini , and Clonorchis sinensis are recognized group 1 carcinogens for their roles in squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder and bile duct cancer (cholangiocarcinoma). We aimed to assess the presence of fluke viruses and their association with malignancy in fluke infections. We showed that all three carcinogenic trematodes harbored related viruses. Focusing on O. viverrini , we observed virus persistence at discrete life stages and viral tropism for the fluke tegument, and we provided molecular and serological evidence of parasitized hosts’ exposure to viral RNA and proteins. Serological analyses confirmed seroconversion of residents in endemic sites and revealed that antibody titers and avidity against fluke-borne viruses increase in individuals with hepatobiliary diseases. Random forest models discriminated efficiently between liver-fluke-infected participants without disease and those with periductal fibrosis or cholangiocarcinoma. Thus, we show that fluke-borne viruses are risk factors and diagnostic targets for fluke-associated cancer.

abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. To model these features, we established an HFpEF mouse model in which sympathetic activation induces hypertensive heart disease, while endothelial dysfunction acts as a second hit driving progression to HFpEF. Hypertensive stress rewires cardiac macrophage-derived intercellular signaling, impairing macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte BMP signaling and fatty acid oxidation while enhancing macrophage-to-fibroblast PDGF signaling, thereby promoting metabolic remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity.

abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) from lung epithelial cells serves as a crucial alarmin to activate the lung-resident group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) and then to initiate type 2 inflammation. However, whether IL-33 has an intrinsic role in the ILC2-driven lung inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we characterize the proteomic features of mouse lung ILC2s during activation and observe an increased expression of intrinsic IL-33 in activated ILC2s. The expression of intrinsic IL-33 in lung ILC2s can be induced by the co-stimulation of cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs) and exogenous IL-33. Deletion of ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 attenuates lung inflammation by restraining ILC2 proliferation and cytokine production. Mechanistically, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 promotes transcriptional activation of both inflammatory and proliferative signaling cascades. Additionally, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 localizes in the nucleus and promotes the expression of Fosl2 and Nfatc1 through promoting their chromatin accessibility, leading to increased ILC2 proliferation and type 2 cytokine production. Further, we confirm that intrinsic IL-33 can be induced by co-stimulation of CysLTs and exogenous IL-33 in human ILC2s (hILC2s), which is positively related to enhanced hILC2 responses. Collectively, our findings implicate IL-33 as a nuclear factor and intrinsic amplifier of lung-resident ILC2s, operating in a positive feedback loop downstream of exogenous IL-33 and CysLTs co-stimulation to promote allergic lung inflammation.

abstract: Epithelial-derived intelectin-1 (ITLN1) is frequently downregulated in colorectal cancer, but whether it actively shapes anti-tumor immunity remains unclear. We integrate multiplex immunohistochemistry, spatial analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, chromatin-accessibility profiling, and perturbation models to define how ITLN1 regulates neutrophil maturation and spatial anti-tumor immunity. In treatment-naïve human colorectal cancer, higher ITLN1 expression associates with greater neutrophil infiltration, shorter distances between mature S100A9 + CXCR2 + neutrophils and ITLN1 + tumor epithelial cells, and improved survival. In mouse colorectal cancer models, Itln1 silencing accelerates tumor growth and metastasis, impairs CXCR2 + CD101 + mature neutrophil generation and tumor recruitment, and promotes LTF + S100A9 + immature neutrophil accumulation in hypoxic regions. Mechanistically, ITLN1 activates a JAK1/STAT3-associated C/EBPδ program that drives terminal granulopoiesis and CXCR2-dependent tumor homing, while recombinant ITLN1 restores neutrophil maturation and tumor-killing activity. Here, we reveal a cross-tissue ITLN1–STAT3/C/EBPδ–CXCR2 axis that links epithelial ITLN1 to bone marrow granulopoiesis, coordinating distal neutrophil maturation, mobilization and spatial organization in colorectal cancer.

abstract: Stem cell–based therapies offer potential for repairing large skeletal defects, yet persistent inflammation limits their efficacy. Here, we identify macrophage–derived IL-18 as an immune switch that impairs skeletal regeneration by disrupting immune–mesenchymal cell interactions. IL-18 is elevated in male mouse non-healing models and human bone nonunion samples, supporting its translational relevance. Mechanistically, IL-18 acts as an upstream amplifier of inflammation by inducing Serpina3f transcription, thereby driving macrophage senescence and M1 polarization and triggering a feed-forward inflammatory cascade that suppresses mesenchymal stem/stromal cell osteogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing and functional assays further show that IL-18 directly impairs mesenchymal stem/stromal cell proliferation, clonogenicity, and mitochondrial fitness. Genetic deletion of IL-18 restores regenerative potential, whereas pharmacological blockade with IL-18–neutralizing antibodies or IL-18 binding protein reverses macrophage dysfunction and promotes bone healing. These findings establish IL-18 as a key mediator of inflammation–induced regenerative failure and a potential therapeutic target for skeletal regeneration.

abstract: Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group ( p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

abstract: Apelin, a hormone secreted by the posterior pituitary, antagonises arginine vasopressin in salt and water homoeostasis. Administration of apelin analogues increased urine output in hyponatremic rodent models, but corresponding human data are lacking. We therefore investigated intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in healthy participants with artificially induced syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis. In this double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study, 15 healthy adults (7 female; mean age, 28 years [SD, 8]) attended three study visits. Hyponatremia was induced using desmopressin, water loading, and hypotonic saline. Participants subsequently received high-dose [Pyr¹]apelin-13 (1800 nmol), low-dose [Pyr¹]apelin-13 (180 nmol), or placebo as a 3-hour infusion. The primary endpoint was cumulative urine output from infusion initiation until 1 hour after its completion. Neither apelin dose produced a clinically relevant difference in urine output compared with placebo. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06277336. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation. Registration number: NCT06277336 .

abstract: Representation learning in genomics often relies on sequence, expression, and network data, thereby overlooking a wealth of insights in the scientific literature. Here, we present LitGene, an interpretable transformer-based model that refines gene representations by integrating unstructured textual information with Gene Ontology annotations through contrastive learning. In evaluations across eight benchmark tasks for protein properties, LitGene achieves competitive accuracy and exhibits zero-shot prediction of GO terms, KEGG pathways, and gene-disease associations. LitGene identified ANGPTL6 as a potential candidate gene for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), supported by its differential expression in independent IPF samples, illustrating LitGene’s utility for hypothesis generation. A SHAP-based interpretability tool highlights text features influencing predictions, while an automated literature-grounding framework provides corroborating support where available. Our results suggest that integrating textual and genetic information may help reduce biases associated with under-studied genes. The model is released as open-source code, along with a publicly accessible web interface at https://litgene.cs.unm.edu/ , which allows users to submit gene names, disease names, drug names, or custom text (e.g., publication abstracts) to obtain evidence-based predictions of related biomedical entities.

abstract: The HIV-1 capsid, composed of capsid (CA) proteins arranged into a conical surface lattice, serves as a critical platform for host–pathogen interactions. Many host cofactors regulate HIV-1 infection by selectively recognizing the higher-order CA lattice rather than individual monomers or capsomers. Among these, Myxovirus resistance protein B (MxB) is a key cellular restriction factor that binds the capsid via its N-terminal fragment containing an arginine-rich motif (RRR), blocking HIV-1 infection at early infection stages. However, the structural basis of this interaction has remained elusive. Here, we present a structural characterization of the CA lattice in complex with the MxB N-terminal fragment using cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging. Combining cryoEM structures with EM-guided all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we identify residue-specific interactions between MxB and the CA trimer interfaces. Notably, residues 10-20 of the MxB N-terminus adopt an α-helical conformation that stabilizes binding at the CA trimer interface, revealing a distinct mode of capsid engagement. These findings provide insight into arginine-rich motif–mediated recognition by MxB and other host factors and establish a structural framework for the development of capsid-targeting antiviral therapeutics.

abstract: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva is a rare genetic disorder caused primarily by the ACVR1 R206H mutation, resulting in debilitating heterotopic ossification triggered by inflammatory flare-ups. Here, we report a disease-modifying, allele-selective small interfering RNA targeting ACVR1 R206H while preserving wildtype ACVR1 function. Docosanoic acid-conjugated ACVR1 small interfering RNA, alone or combined with one targeting the pro-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-1β, reduced heterotopic ossification in a murine model using both post-trauma and preventative strategies. Combination therapy was more effective than either pathway alone. We further developed lipophilic divalent molecules targeting both pathways in a single compound. These showed comparable muscle accumulation and efficacy to the combined monovalent forms following local and systemic administration, while enabling equimolar dosing and simplified manufacturing. Treatment suppressed inflammatory, WNT, Notch, Hedgehog, and transforming growth factor β signaling in fibroadipogenic progenitors, reducing cartilage, bone, and connective tissue formation. This work establishes a platform for disease-modifying therapies in this and other musculoskeletal disorders.

abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring in interstitial fluid (ISF) is important for diabetes management, but enzyme-based sensors can lose activity, while many nonenzymatic alternatives show optimal activity in alkaline media. Here we present a regenerable wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform for closed-loop nonenzymatic ISF glucose monitoring. Negative pressure extracts ISF into a detachable sensor cartridge that separates the tissue interface from the electrochemical sensing chamber and enables rinsing and reuse. A brief cathodic step triggers the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at an Au–Pt/Ni foam electrode, electrochemically generating a local alkaline interface for the subsequent glucose oxidation reaction (GOR). Integrated pH feedback regulates the HER–GOR sequence. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate rapid ISF extraction and quasi-continuous glucose monitoring in rats, with preliminary feasibility in one human participant. This work illustrates local microenvironment regulation as a strategy for enabling alkaline-dependent glucose electrocatalysis in near-neutral ISF.

abstract: Most characterized anti-CRISPR proteins act via well-defined core inhibitory mechanisms, yet how auxiliary structural elements modulate and potentiate these canonical processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that AcrIIC1 Boe represses Nme1Cas9 activity through an integrated, loop-coupled regulatory mode. Based on canonical occlusion of the HNH catalytic site, the extended loop of AcrIIC1 Boe provides an additional coupled regulatory layer to remodel sgRNA spacer arrangement and R-loop progression, thereby enhancing Cas9 inhibition. Loop deletion largely abrogates robust inhibition, indicating that this loop module is indispensable for full AcrIIC1 inhibitory potency. Consistently, transplantation of this functional loop into the weakly active AcrIIC1 Nme1 efficiently elevates its inhibitory performance. Our findings identify a loop-mediated regulatory strategy that potentiates the canonical HNH occlusion mechanism, clarify the structural basis for functional divergence across AcrIIC1 homologs, and offer a modular engineering principle for the rational design and optimization of anti-CRISPR proteins with enhanced potency.

abstract: Despite significant climate variability in the Northern Hemisphere ~50,000–12,000 years ago, the potential for vertebrates to periodically thrive in the glacial Arctic Ocean has been largely overlooked because ecosystem productivity was assumed to be too low. Here, we analyze fish otoliths preserved in deep-sea sediments and find that two Arctic endemic cod species, ice cod ( Arctogadus glacialis ) and polar cod ( Boreogadus saida ), lived at 87–89 °N ~ 48,000–35,000 years ago and reappeared at the onset of the Holocene ~12,000 years ago. A. glacialis also occurred north of Greenland at 84–85 °N ~ 20,000 years ago, during the peak of the Last Glacial Maximum, suggesting the presence of refugia that enabled survival and divergence from B. saida under the harshest climate conditions. These findings suggest that the glacial Arctic Ocean was not a barren ice desert but rather a breeding ground for the evolution of cold adaptation in marine fish.

abstract: Evidence on real-world effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccination during pregnancy remains limited. Using health data from the UK, Sweden, Spain, and Norway, we emulated two target trials to estimate vaccine effectiveness (VE) of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines administered during pregnancy against COVID-19 infection, hospitalisation, and admission to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU). The first trial compares initiation of a primary (two-dose) vaccination with unvaccinated, and the second compares the receipt of a first booster (third dose) with unboosted after primary vaccination. Pregnant women receiving a first or booster vaccination were matched weekly to comparable unexposed pregnant women. A total of 62,061 and 41,096 pregnant women were included in the first and second trial, respectively. Meta-analysis across the four databases showed a VE for primary vaccination of 26·2% (95% CI 16·2–35·1) against infection and 55·6% (95% CI 44·1–64·8) against hospitalisation. For boosters, the VE was 33.6% (95% CI 1·6–56·6) against infection and 34·1% (95% CI 0·6–56·4) against hospitalisation. ICU admission outcomes were too rare to analyse. In this work, we show that primary and first-booster mRNA vaccination during pregnancy is associated to a lower risk of COVID-19-related hospitalisation, while protection against infection is more modest and heterogeneous across databases.

abstract: Prostate cancer is a common malignancy with a heterogeneous disease course. Prior studies have identified a paucity of point mutations in protein-coding genes and only a few clinically relevant driver alterations. Here, using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole genome sequencing dataset from 1001 men, we perform an integrative analysis of cancer driver genes by quantifying recurrent genomic alterations among small mutations, structural variants, and copy number alterations in 961 primary prostate tumour samples. We identify at least one recurrent somatic or germline alteration in 97% of tumours and identify putative driver genes and mechanisms of dysregulation including frequently altered regulatory elements. A prominent example is the activation of oncogenes by structural variation-mediated hijacking of onco-enhancers of the solute carrier gene family including SLC30A4 . Other recurrent alterations including FOXA1, MDM4, COL5A1, TP53 , and BRCA1 stratify with metastatic disease, with additional drivers enriched in African-ancestry tumours. One quarter of tumours have acquired genome-informed therapeutic targets. Unsupervised analysis of alterations reveals four oncotypes with distinct genetic and clinical characteristics, including two clinically unfavourable oncotypes with shorter metastasis-free survival. Our study uncovers the full spectrum and recurrence patterns of genomic driver alterations in primary prostate cancers and delivers targets for biomarker development, mechanistic studies, and potential therapeutic interventions.

abstract: To protect themselves against phage infection, bacteria employ diverse defense systems that are typically activated specifically upon infection. However, the mechanisms of activation and self versus non-self discrimination for most systems remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the bacterial immunity protein DARNA, once activated, cleaves a subset of host tRNAs, thereby inhibiting phage propagation. Although phages escape DARNA-mediated defense through mutations in the gene encoding single-stranded DNA-binding protein (SSB), we find that phage SSBs do not directly stimulate DARNA. Instead, DARNA is activated by single-stranded DNA presented by phage SSB, but not by the host SSB. The recognition of an endogenous nucleic acid signal promoted by a viral protein ensures that DARNA can detect and respond to a broad range of viruses while avoiding autoimmunity.

abstract: Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage–fusion–bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. Validation across 175 metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization-probed genes in 72 models demonstrated accurate predictions. Analysis of 6,506 patient pan-cancer samples revealed ecDNA-mediated oncogene co-amplification preferences. To democratize data sharing, we created AmpliconRepository, a community-contributable platform, enabling investigation of results across >15,000 publicly hosted samples.

abstract: Since the discovery and application of green fluorescent protein for use as an optical tag, fluorescent proteins (FPs) have changed the way we observe biological signals and processes. FP and fluorescent biosensor design has continued to advance, facilitated by new technologies and developments in chemistry, physics, engineering and screening technologies. We summarize some of the recent developments in FP engineering, focusing on insights that have led to improved photostability or longer wavelengths, among other improvements, highlighting mScarlet as a case study. We also discuss the engineering of new fluorescent biosensors, focusing on the ways in which screening, quantitative imaging, spatial resolution and multiplexing have been improved in recent years. Finally, we conclude with a perspective on what the future holds for the next generation of FPs and biosensors.

title: Raphe nuclei in cognition: A network-level framework for behavioral-state control.
An ancient polymorphism in myosin I a/b determines chiral variation in Japanese Euhadra snails.

journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Global origins of tuna and billfish fisheries reveal the transition from coastal access to oceanic exploitation.
abstract: Ocean ecosystems have played a crucial role in people's lives around the world for millennia. However, questions persist about when, why, and how people first began removing biomass from offshore habitats and established fisheries in distant, oceanic environments. We explore the antiquity and evolution of tuna (Thunnini) and billfish (Istiophoridae/Xiphiidae) fisheries, two groups of fishes that occur around the world, are economically significant, and are ecologically important open ocean apex predators. The earliest archaeological evidence of fishing for tuna occurs ~44,000 years ago and billfish at ~10,000 years ago, with early fisheries for some tuna species appearing around the world by 3,000 to 1,000 years ago. Most early fisheries are in areas where tunas and billfishes could be accessed relatively close to shore (e.g., submarine canyons) and/or where these fishes may come inshore seasonally or during warm ocean events. Early tuna and billfish fisheries were often linked to ceremony/ritual, alongside advances in maritime technologies. With few exceptions, sustained and intensive commercial exploitation of pelagic predators in offshore and oceanic habitats is a late development in the human past, occurring primarily during the last 200 y. Our findings document a long-term continuum of human interactions with global marine ecosystems spanning thousands of years, including significant differences between the timing and pathways by which people became dominant ecological drivers in nearshore compared to offshore/oceanic ecosystems.

title: Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific protein coronas and immune cell interactions.
abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and modulate nanoparticle-cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano-bio interface. Herein, we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent immune cell interactions are substantially reduced following protein corona formation, although differences among polymer chemistries persist. Zwitterionic coatings broadly suppress immune cell interactions, whereas PEG-based coatings preferentially promote interactions with antigen-presenting cells. These findings establish design principles for polymer-functionalized nanoparticles with specific immune cell interaction profiles.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Thermal imbalance drives avian performance and responses to climate warming.
abstract: Thermal performance curves are widely used to predict ectothermic responses to climate warming but are less effective for predicting endotherm performance across environmental conditions because thermoregulation often decouples body temperature from ambient temperature. We develop theory and provide empirical evidence for performance curves in endotherms structured by net sensible heat flux (Q), an integrative index of thermoregulatory imbalance. Using biophysical simulations in tree swallows, we show that performance varies predictably with Q (which we term "QPCs"), thereby explaining variation in nestling provisioning performance, reproductive fitness, and geographic limits, while also forecasting responses to climate change. We also demonstrate that thermal imbalance helps shape breeding ranges of birds across North America. Our findings introduce Q as a broadly relevant ecophysiological dimension that constrains performance in endotherms and provides a framework for predicting endotherm responses to climate warming.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Dynamic partitioning shapes the in vivo organization of the Escherichia coli RNA degradosome.
abstract: The bacterial RNA degradosome is a central mediator of RNA turnover, yet how its components are organized and regulated in living cells remains unclear. Using live-cell single-molecule imaging, we quantified the spatial distribution and dynamics of the four major Escherichia coli degradosome components: RNase E, RhlB, PNPase, and enolase. These proteins occupied distinct membrane-associated and cytoplasmic pools whose relative abundance varied among proteins and changed with physiological state. In particular, PNPase underwent pronounced redistribution between membrane-associated and cytoplasmic states in response to altered RNA availability and growth conditions, whereas RNase E and RhlB remained largely membrane associated. To determine the functional consequences of this organization, we examined the degradation of lacZ reporter transcripts with different translation initiation strengths. PNPase and RhlB preferentially promoted degradation of weakly translated transcripts, whereas strongly translated transcripts were largely insensitive to their loss. Together, these results reveal that the bacterial RNA degradosome is not a static, uniformly assembled molecular machine. Instead, RNA decay is organized through dynamic intracellular partitioning of degradosome components, linking physiological state and translation status to transcript degradation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: A transposon inserted into HELD1 repressed maize husk leaf blade extension during maize domestication.
abstract: Husk leaves are the closest photosynthetic organs to the ear, which contribute directly to grain filling and have potential for yield improvement in maize. Teosinte has a long husk extended leaf blade, whereas maize exhibits a reduced or even no husk leaf blade. However, the genetic basis of this transition in the husk leaf during domestication remains unknown. In this study, we identified a major quantitative trait locus (QTL), Husk Extended Leaf Blade 1 (HELD1), corresponding to the tassels replace upper ears1 (tru1) gene. A 133-base pair (bp) Harbinger transposon inserted into the tru1 intron introduces two TEOSINTE BRANCHED 1 (TB1) binding motifs, thereby recruiting TB1 to directly enhance tru1 transcription. Further analyses revealed that TRU1 interacts with the transcription factor ALOG1, which in turn enhances the expression of liguleless2 (lg2), a key regulator of ligule development. Together with brassinosteroid-deficient dwarf1 (brd1) and GA2ox1, these genes set up a regulatory network that defines the ligular-auricular position, controls the leaf blade-to-husk (sheath) ratio in husk and stem leaves, and regulates husk leaf blade length. Population genetic analyses indicate that HELD1 experienced significant human selection, resulting in the transposon insertion becoming the dominant allele in domesticated maize. Additionally, the teosinte HELD1 allele with extended husk leaf blades significantly enhances yield in maize. Our results demonstrate HELD1 is an important regulator of husk and stem leaf architectures, contributing to the ligular-auricular position to adjust the ratio of leaf blade to husk or sheath.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Physical origins of speed control in swimming fishes.
abstract: The linear relationship between tail-beat frequency and swimming speed in fish, first described by Bainbridge in 1958, has since been confirmed in species as disparate as eels and tuna. Dimensional scaling has explained why linearity should emerge at high Reynolds numbers, but the frequency-speed relationship itself has remained empirical, with no physical framework describing its behavior across swimming regimes, and no account of what sets the two quantities that define it: the distance covered per tail beat and the frequency below which forward motion supposedly ceases. Here, we derive a relationship from a balance of fin thrust, generated by a leading-edge vortex, and drag due to the boundary layer on the body. This framework yields an explicit expression for speed in terms of midline kinematics and body morphology. This formulation shows that the maximum stride length is set by the undulatory wavelength and the tail-beat phase offset, rather than by the conventional scaling metric of body length, and that no minimum frequency is required for forward motion. The model reproduces kinematic measurements from freely swimming glass catfish, published simulations, and Bainbridge's original data. Without recalibration, it predicts the results of independent simulations spanning wide variations in wavelength, phase offset, and morphology to within ten percent. Linear scaling is thus one asymptotic limit of a more general propulsive relationship linking morphology and body-wave kinematics to swimming speed in fishes and bioinspired vehicles, where the body waveform, rather than the actuation frequency, emerges as the variable that sets performance.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Insights from coproduced scenarios toward urban sustainability transformations.
abstract: Urban sustainability transformations call for fundamental shifts in how cities are organized, developed, and governed. Yet we need a better understanding of the diversity of visions and pathways that can enable transformative change. We address this gap through an analysis of 60 coproduced positive scenario visions and pathways developed using the Sustainable Future Scenario process, across nine US and Latin American cities participating in the Urban Resilience to Extremes Sustainability Research Network. We engaged diverse urban stakeholders-including government, nonprofit, and private decision-makers, community leaders, residents, and academic collaborators-in more than 20 coproduction workshops to explore alternative urban futures of sustainability and resilience. We examined how the coproduced scenarios represent five domains of transformative change (nature-human relationships, economic transformation, governance, social and environmental justice, and infrastructure futures) and four theories of transformative change (structural/institutional, agency/power, goals of the system, and worldviews/values). Most pathways combined multiple theories of change operating across multiple domains, revealing urban transformations as entangled rather than singular interventions. Some strategies were common across cities-car-free regions, decentralized infrastructure, community-based governance, expanded fundamental rights-yet were pursued with different transformative aims, demonstrating how a strategy's transformative intent depends on the theories of change behind it. These findings position coproduced scenarios as more than a normative or planning tool and offer an analytical approach for surfacing the possibility space of urban transformation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Poly(phenolic) deposition is a prerequisite to poly(aliphatic) deposition for functional potato suberin.
abstract: Suberin deposition in specialized cells is a critical aspect of plant protection, providing both water retention and pathogen protection functions. Tissue specific suberization during plant development is mirrored by its wound induction in cells that do not normally suberize and provides a robust experimental system to investigate the process. Suberized cells are characterized by a cell wall-associated lignin-like poly(phenolic) domain, and an ester-linked poly(aliphatic) domain, with the latter often laid down in distinct lamellar bands between the cell wall and plasma membrane. Previous work provides evidence that poly(phenolic) deposition precedes, and is necessary for, poly(aliphatic) deposition. To test this further, we generated RNAi knockdown lines of three wound-induced peroxidase genes, PRX19, PRX55, and PRX105, in potato (Solanum tuberosum), the tubers of which produce an abundance of suberin upon wounding. Peroxidases catalyze the oxidative free radical coupling of phenolic monomers to form the suberin poly(phenolic) domain. The wound-induced suberin of PRX19-RNAi tubers had severely reduced poly(phenolics), reduced poly(aliphatics), and no apparent lamella. Functionally, wound-induced PRX19-RNAi tubers were more permeable to water loss and susceptible to bacterial soft rot. Overall, our data support the hypothesis that poly(phenolic) domain assembly is a strict requirement for subsequent deposition of aliphatic lamella within wound-induced suberin.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Modulation of avian iridescence via melanogenesis.
abstract: The iridescent colors of birds originate in nanoscale feather structures that interact with light. Although the physical principles governing avian iridescence are well established, the molecular mechanisms assembling these nanostructures into photonic materials remain unknown. Here, we integrated genomic, cellular, and optical approaches to investigate the molecular basis of iridescent color formation in birds. We leveraged mutations that arose in the domesticated Indian peafowl and natural color variation in wild birds. In peafowl, we identified eight genes underlying gains, losses, and shifts of iridescence, whereas in two wild species, we used single-cell transcriptomics to profile asymmetric feathers in which iridescent and noniridescent barbules develop on opposite sides of the same feather. We found that all peafowl mutations mapped to melanogenesis genes, showing that variation in this pathway can modify diverse geometric features of feather photonic nanostructures. Mutations altering melanin composition collapsed multilayered photonic systems and yielded noniridescent tissues, whereas changes in melanosome abundance, elongation, or deposition timing generated multilayer architectures with variable periodicity and color. We further show in peafowl that transitions from noniridescent to iridescent plumage were associated with single-nucleotide mutations in a melanogenesis gene, suggesting that, in species already capable of forming multilayered nanostructures, iridescence can be gained by relatively small genetic changes. Single-cell transcriptomes from wild species also supported extensive melanocyte-centered regulatory rewiring associated with iridescence, including changes in melanosome maturation, trafficking, and intercellular signaling. Together, these results show that the nanoscale order underlying iridescence is developmentally plastic and highly responsive to the melanogenic environment.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: A conserved Hox9-10 code underlies the early establishment of hind appendage progenitors in zebrafish and the Iberian ribbed newt.
abstract: The acquisition of paired appendages was a key innovation in vertebrate evolution. Although HoxA/D paralog groups (PGs) 9-13 play central roles in patterning paired fins and limbs, the evolutionary origin of this paired appendage-patterning system remains unknown. Here, we show that HoxA/D PG9-10 genes are essential for the early establishment of pelvic fin progenitors in zebrafish, and that Hox9-10 function is similarly required for hindlimb progenitor formation in the Iberian ribbed newt. In zebrafish, combined disruption of five HoxA/D PG9-10 genes abolishes the detectable pelvic fin progenitor population, resulting in complete loss of pelvic fins. A Tg(hoxa10b:EGFP) reporter labeled cells in the presumptive pelvic fin field before pelvic fin bud formation. Importantly, simultaneous CRISPR-mediated disruption of all seven Hox9-10 paralogs in the Iberian ribbed newt similarly impaired the establishment of hindlimb progenitors, suggesting that an early requirement for Hox9-10 function in hind appendage development predates the divergence of ray-finned and lobe-finned vertebrates. Together, these findings identify an evolutionarily conserved role for posterior Hox9-10 genes in the initial establishment of hind appendage progenitors. Because overlapping posterior Hox paralog groups are subsequently deployed during paired appendage patterning, this early Hox9-10 requirement provides a developmental link between the posterior axial Hox code and the paired appendage-patterning system. Our results are therefore consistent with the hypothesis that recruitment of a posterior Hox code into hind appendage progenitor formation contributed to the evolutionary assembly of the vertebrate paired appendage-patterning system.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Altered sperm DNA methylation provides an epigenetic route from overweight and older men to intergenerational disease transmission.
abstract: The occurrence of childhood neurodevelopmental disorders has been steadily increasing for decades, yet we have little understanding of modes of inheritance implicated in these diseases. Epidemiology studies have revealed an association between an elevated paternal Body Mass Index (BMI) and age as factors implicated in increased risk for neurodevelopmental disorders in children. Epigenetic regulation of gene expression by DNA methylation at cytosines is susceptible to environmental, diet, and lifestyle changes. Yet, whether a man's BMI and age influence the sperm methylome and potentially impact offspring development remains unresolved. Using MethylC capture sequencing, we identified over 38,000 differentially methylated CpGs in the sperm of men with an elevated BMI, with overlap occurring in regions associated with advanced paternal age. These were enriched for neural gene and disease ontologies. Differentially methylated regions localized to transposable elements that can act as active enhancers during human zygotic genome activation, and at gene promoters for early lineage specification. These results suggest that sperm methylome alterations that are linked to an elevated BMI may influence key embryonic transcriptional processes, notably those associated with trophectoderm and placental development.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Loss of tRNA uridine thiolation affects mRNA translation, protein production, and metabolite accumulation in Arabidopsis.
abstract: It is well established in yeast and animal system that the level of uridine thiolation at position 34 of tRNA anticodon loops can impact the decoding potential of the corresponding codons. Using Arabidopsis thaliana, we confirm that the ability of the plant ribosome to decode AAA, GAA, and CAA codons is impaired when this thiol group is lost, leading to a reduction in protein production, especially for genes enriched in these codons. Interestingly, we observed that loss of tRNA thiolation results in variations in the levels of numerous proteins involved in sulfur-compound metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These variations, in turn, affect the accumulation of several sulfur-containing metabolites and amino acids, suggesting that the level of tRNA thiolation has a direct and profound impact on plant metabolism. We also demonstrate that U34 thiolation is essential for adjusting plant growth in response to sulfur limitation and that its absence directly affects the plant's interaction with bacteria, including both pathogens and beneficial organisms. Our results support the hypothesis that the level of tRNA thiolation can be used in plant to link nutritional status to translation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: A "knob-in-hole" gate in the antibody C(H)1 domain underlies subclass-independent IgA hinge cleavage by the commensal metallopeptidase IgAse.
abstract: Human immunoglobulin (Ig) A (IgA) protects ≈400 m2 of mucosae from microbes. Bacterial IgA-peptidases subvert this defense by cleaving the Fab-Fc hinge of subclass IgA1 while sparing the hinge-divergent, colon-dominant IgA2 subclass. The exception is IgAse, a ≈140-kDa, seven-domain, membrane-bound metallopeptidase from the colonic commensal Thomasclavelia ramosa that targets both subclasses but no other protein. We previously narrowed the minimal functional assembly down to the IgAse catalytic and wrapping domains (CD and WD) plus the IgA1/2 Fab', i.e., the hinge and a Fab of light and heavy chains (LC, HC), each with a variable and a constant Ig domain (VL + CL, VH + CH1). The transient interaction culminates in cleavage of a proline-valine bond within the first two hinge residues, downstream of a conserved C-terminal CH1 disulfide (SS2). Here, single-particle cryoelectron microscopy of a disulfide-stabilized minimal IgAse:IgA2 Fab' complex yielded high-quality density strongly supporting two states along the cleavage reaction coordinate, a "recognition complex" and a subsequent "precatalytic complex," in which Fab' binds frontally to the IgAse CD via a CH1 β-sheet and overhang loop LβEβF. This loop binds like a knob to a preformed hole in the active-site cleft. Binding rearranges the knob and rotates SS2 ≈ 180°, enabling access of the hinge into the cleft of the otherwise unaffected precatalytic complex. Together, this work defines a unique, CH1-mediated hinge-delivering "gate" mechanism, validated by a crystal structure of unbound IgA2 Fab, point mutations disrupting the CH1:CD interface, and molecular dynamics calculations, which provide the structural framework for subclass-independent IgA cleavage.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Quiescence to proliferation transition regulates asynchronous mitochondrial DNA replication dynamics.
abstract: Each human cell contains hundreds to thousands of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copies, only a small fraction of which replicates independently of the cell cycle. An asynchronous replication of the leading and lagging strands has been proposed to represent a major replication mode in mitochondria, complicating the investigation of mechanisms that regulate mtDNA replication. Using single-DNA-molecule analysis that distinguishes the origins and timing of replication of each strand, we show that the mitochondrial DNA replication machinery responds to the transition from quiescence to proliferation by dynamically dissociating strand-specific replication rates and modulating the physiological requirements for factors involved in replication and transcription. During this response, the requirement for mitochondrial RNA polymerase (POLRMT) in replication initiation increases, whereas that for primase-polymerase (PrimPol), which is thought to function in DNA repriming at DNA lesions, eventually decreases. Thus, precise quantification of mtDNA replication rates at the single-strand level reveals the temporally dynamic nature of the mtDNA replication machinery during the transition from quiescence to proliferation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Nitrogen deposition does not alter the temperate forest soil carbon pool: A 14-y experiment on varied nitrogen fertilization.
abstract: Soil carbon (C) pools in nitrogen-limited temperate forests are critical to the global C cycle, but there are no long-term experiments examining soil C, with various nitrogen (N) forms. Here, a 14-y experiment (100 kg N ha-1 y-1), with added N simulating atmospheric deposition proportions (~70% inorganic, ~30% organic) did not affect soil C pools, whereas organic N (ON) and inorganic N (IN) individually significantly increased values by 2.7-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively. Although no treatment significantly affected soil pH, treatment effects on pH were negatively associated with soil C pools. In addition, treatments containing ON forms increased mineral-associated organic C fractions, indicating enhanced C stability vs. IN. These findings enhance our understanding of N deposition-soil C pool interactions.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome-mitochondrion Ca(2+) transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi.
abstract: Calcium ion (Ca2+) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in Trypanosoma cruzi, the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome-mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca2+ transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca2+ release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca2+ uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca2+ uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca2+ transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca2+ transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Efficient and accurate steering of large language models through attention-guided feature learning.
abstract: Activation steering, or direct manipulation of internal activations to guide large language model (LLM) responses toward specific semantic concepts, is emerging as a promising avenue for both understanding how semantic concepts are stored within LLMs and advancing LLM capabilities. Yet, existing steering methods are remarkably brittle, with seemingly nonsteerable concepts becoming completely steerable based on subtle algorithmic choices in how concept-related features are extracted. In this work, we introduce an attention-guided framework for activation steering that overcomes three core challenges associated with steering: 1) automatic selection of relevant token embeddings for extracting concept-related features; 2) accounting for heterogeneity of concept-related features across LLM activations; and 3) identification of layers most relevant for steering. Across a steering benchmark of 512 semantic concepts, our framework substantially improved steering over previous state-of-the-art (nearly doubling the number of successfully steered concepts) across model architectures and sizes (up to 70 billion parameter models). Furthermore, we use our framework to shed light on the distribution of concept-specific features across LLM layers. Overall, our framework opens further avenues for developing efficient, highly scalable fine-tuning algorithms for industry-scale LLMs.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: A neural operator framework for data-driven discovery of stability and receptivity in physical systems.
abstract: Understanding how complex systems respond to perturbations, such as whether they will remain stable or what their most sensitive patterns are, is a fundamental challenge across science and engineering. Traditional stability and receptivity (resolvent) analyses are powerful but rely on known equations and linearization, limiting their use in nonlinear or poorly modeled systems. Here, we introduce a data-driven framework that automatically identifies stability properties of both equilibrium points and periodic orbits, as well as optimal forcing responses from observation data alone, without requiring governing equations. By training a neural network as a dynamics emulator and using automatic differentiation to extract its Jacobian, we can perform stability and receptivity analyses directly from data. We demonstrate the method on systems of increasing complexity, from canonical models to high-dimensional fluid flows and a real-world climate dataset, employing model reduction where needed and successfully identifying dominant instability modes and optimal input-output structures, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. By leveraging a neural network emulator, we readily obtain a nonlinear representation of system dynamics while additionally retrieving intricate dynamical patterns that were previously difficult to resolve. This equation-free methodology establishes a broadly applicable tool for analyzing complex, high-dimensional datasets, with potential relevance to grand challenges in fields such as climate science, neuroscience, and fluid engineering.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: PCS-UQ: Uncertainty quantification via the Predictability-Computability-Stability framework.
abstract: As machine learning (ML) enters high-stakes domains, trustworthy uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for safety. In this paper we introduce PCS-UQ, a framework based on the predictability, computability, and stability (PCS) principles for veridical data science. Starting with a candidate set of models or algorithms, PCS-UQ integrates a rigorous prediction-check to screen out unsuitable models in the set and utilizes bootstrap samples in order to capture both inter-sample variability and algorithmic instability for the prediction-checked algorithms. We then introduce a multiplicative calibration scheme to enhance local adaptivity, which can be viewed as a score function in conformal prediction. Moreover, we produce a compilation of 17 real-world regression datasets with manually constructed subgroups. On this benchmark, PCS-UQ maintains the target coverage while outperforming or matching conformal methods equipped with oracle-selected algorithms in interval width. PCS-UQ achieves consistent subgroup coverage, outperforming these oracle-selected conformal methods. Notably, PCS-UQ stands out in achieving both competitive interval widths and consistent subgroup coverage. Across six classification datasets, PCS-UQ reduces prediction set sizes by 20%. To scale the framework for deep learning, we propose computationally efficient variants that bypass expensive retraining. On three computer vision benchmarks, these variants reduce prediction set sizes by 20% over conformal baselines. Finally, we provide a theoretical proof that a modified PCS-UQ algorithm preserves valid coverage under exchangeability as a form of split conformal inference.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Nuclear BbAtg8 interacts with BbMac1 as a transcriptional modulator to sustain nuclear copper homeostasis during conidial germination.
abstract: Pathogenic fungi endure host impose copper starvation by tightly coordinating trace metal homeostasis. However, how pathogens synchronize endogenous metal recycling with exogenous copper uptake to promote infection remains enigmatic. Using the entomopathogenic fungus Beauveria bassiana, we uncovered a synergistic regulatory network that prioritizes nuclear copper enrichment during conidial germination. Under copper deprivation, the fungus deploys a highly coordinated dual-track survival strategy. In the cytoplasm, the core autophagy protein BbAtg8 drives autophagic flux, specifically triggering mitophagy to degrade mitochondria, thereby promoting the turnover and mobilization of endogenous copper stores. Concurrently, a nonlipidated pool of BbAtg8 translocates to the nucleus to coordinate exogenous uptake. Within the nucleus, BbAtg8 directly interacts with the copper-fist transcription factor BbMac1 via a functional Atg8-interacting motif (AIM). This physical interaction serves as a potent transcriptional modulator, significantly enhancing BbMac1's DNA-binding affinity. Consequently, the Atg8-Mac1 complex hyper-activates the expression of three functionally redundant copper transporters (BbCtr1, BbCtr2, and BbCtr4) to aggressively absorb extracellular copper. Strikingly, severe copper deprivation triggers a dynamic spatial enrichment of these classical copper transporters at the nuclear envelope, which correlates with the sustained maintenance of nuclear copper homeostasis required for essential genomic functions and full fungal virulence. Together, these findings reveal how pathogens synchronize mitophagy-mediated endogenous turnover with Mac1-driven exogenous uptake, fundamentally expanding the role of autophagy proteins BbAtg8 into direct transcriptional coordinators of metal homeostasis. This dual-track regulatory model not only deepens our understanding of fungal adaptation to nutritional immunity but also provides potential targets for disrupting copper homeostasis to control fungal pathogens.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: AI can persuade people to take political actions.
abstract: There is substantial concern about the ability of advanced AI to influence people's behavior. A rapidly growing body of research has found that AI can produce large persuasive effects on people's attitudes, but whether AI can persuade people to take consequential real-world actions has remained unclear. In two large preregistered experiments ([Formula: see text] responses from 14,779 people), we used conversational AI models to persuade participants on a range of attitudinal and behavioral outcomes, including signing real petitions and donating money to charity. We found sizable AI persuasion effects on these behavioral outcomes (e.g. [Formula: see text]19.7 percentage points on petition signing). However, we observed no evidence of a correlation between AI persuasion effects on attitudes and effects on behavior. Moreover, we replicated prior findings that information provision drove effects on attitudes, but found no such evidence for our behavioral outcomes. In a test of eight behavioral persuasion strategies, the strategy focused on information provision produced the smallest behavioral effect, though differences among the eight were small. Taken together, these results suggest that previous findings relying on attitudinal outcomes may generalize poorly to behavior, and therefore risk substantially mischaracterizing the real-world behavioral impact of AI persuasion.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: A promoter G-quadruplex recruits Hrb27C to regulate NEMO and immune defense against Lyme disease pathogens in the deer tick.
abstract: Genomic DNA can adopt noncanonical secondary structures, such as G-quadruplexes (G4s), which serve as critical regulatory elements beyond the traditional double helix. Whether promoter G4s also participate in controlling innate immune signaling and host-pathogen interactions, however, remains unknown in arthropods. In this study, we identify a G4 structure within the promoter of the NEMO (NF-κB essential modulator) gene in the deer tick Ixodes scapularis. Using a combination of circular dichroism, isothermal difference spectra, and fluorescence-based assays, we demonstrate that this sequence forms a stable, parallel G4 topology in vitro and in vivo. Functional characterization via luciferase reporter assays reveals that this G4 scaffold is essential for proper NEMO transcriptional output. Importantly, disruption of the G4 structure significantly reduces NEMO expression and increases the burden of the Lyme disease spirochete Borrelia burgdorferi. Genome-wide expression profiling further reveals that perturbation of the NEMO G4 produces transcriptional changes that overlap with those observed following NEMO silencing. These shared transcriptional responses are enriched for immune-associated genes and ribonucleoprotein-related pathways. We further identify the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein Hrb27C as a structural binding protein that specifically recognizes the NEMO G4 through its RNA recognition motif domains and facilitates NEMO expression. Collectively, our findings establish promoter G4 architecture as an important regulatory layer in tick immunity, linking DNA topology to pathogen proliferation and providing a structural framework for understanding host-pathogen dynamics in disease vectors.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: A muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein regulates postnatal heart growth through mitonuclear ubiquinone-PPAR signaling.
abstract: Increased mitochondrial biogenesis and aerobic respiration in postnatal mammalian organs are essential for adaptation to extrauterine life, yet the functions of many tissue-enriched, developmentally regulated mitochondrial proteins remain poorly defined.
