By integrating mitochondrial proteome annotations with mouse and human transcriptomic datasets, we identified Coenzyme Q10a (Coq10a), a striated muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein, as a regulator of postnatal cardiac growth. Coq10a, the mammalian homolog of the yeast ubiquinone-binding protein Coq10p, is highly induced in the heart after birth through thyroid hormone-, Nkx2.5-, and Tbx5-dependent regulation. To define its physiological function, we generated three independent Coq10a-deficient mouse models. Both global and cardiomyocyte-specific loss of Coq10a promoted postnatal cardiac hypertrophy without impairing basal cardiac function or mitochondrial respiration. Instead, Coq10a deficiency altered intracellular ubiquinone partitioning, resulting in increased ubiquinone accumulation in a microsomal membrane fraction. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of PPAR-associated metabolic gene sets and induction of established PPAR-responsive genes in Coq10a-deficient hearts. Pharmacological inhibition of PPARα and PPARγ, but not PPARδ, attenuated the hypertrophic phenotype. Molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and mutagenesis identified PPARα residues that contribute to differential responsiveness to ubiquinone. Although Coq10a-deficient hearts maintained near-normal function under basal conditions, they exhibited increased susceptibility to pressure-overload stress. Together, these findings establish Coq10a as a regulator of intracellular ubiquinone partitioning and support a model linking altered mitochondrial lipid distribution and PPAR-associated signaling to postnatal cardiac growth. More broadly, they demonstrate how tissue-enriched mitochondrial proteins can mediate organ-specific physiological functions beyond energy production.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine triggers an adaptive response that extends lifespan through the YBT1 ABC transporter.
abstract: S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) is a fundamental methyl donor; however, the physiological role of its byproduct and competitive inhibitor, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH), remains unclear. Here, we show that transient reactive oxygen species (ROS) production triggered by SAH during the early logarithmic phase mimics partial SAH hydrolase inhibition, extending the yeast chronological lifespan (CLS) through a hormetic mechanism. This study reveals that the dual nature of ROS in aging is determined by the specific degree of SAH hydrolase activity. We identified the adenosine 5'-triphosphate-binding cassette (ABC) transporter Ybt1 as a key downstream effector of SAH. Ybt1 localizes to the vacuolar membrane and facilitates the sequestration of SAM from the cytosol into the vacuole. Notably, YBT1 overexpression extends CLS, mimicking SAH effects through an integrated pathway involving target of rapamycin complex 1 downregulation, autophagy, and adenosine 5'-monophosphate-activated protein kinase activation. Our findings establish that SAH acts as a metabolic signal coupling nutrient and energy availability to longevity via Ybt1, defining an adaptive/hormetic response for lifespan regulation in yeast.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Systemic collapse emergence from climate-induced perturbations in transportation networks.
abstract: The interaction between human infrastructures and external events results in loss of functionality or even complete system disruption through a snowball effect of cascading failures. Their complex interplay challenges their prevention, affecting the human population that rely on their functionality. Understanding how these networks respond to external perturbations is crucial for predicting and mitigating the impacts of disruptive events. In particular, meteorological events, while not preventable, can have significant impacts on human infrastructure. Here, we propose a model coupling the dynamics of transportation systems to the dynamics of external events considered as fields, to capture at the same time the critical behavior of the former and the level of influence of the latter. The impact of rainfalls on real-world railway networks provides a compelling case study, showcasing local endemic and system-wide disruptions above a critical value of the rainfall strength. Remarkably, localized perturbations on the wider network reveals the local weaknesses of the global infrastructure, and we assess them in terms of system perturbability and corresponding societal risk. Our framework opens the door to the quantitative analysis of criticalities in essential human infrastructure imputable to vulnerabilities that are set to intensify due to climate change.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Omega-3 fatty acids reprogram tumor-associated macrophage cytokine signaling and suppress pancreatic cancer growth.
abstract: Dietary polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) shape inflammatory signaling within the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), but the cellular mechanisms underlying their effects on tumor progression remain unclear. Using orthotopic models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), we show that omega-3 (n-3) and omega-6 (n-6) PUFAs are differentially incorporated into tumor lipid pools, generating spatially heterogeneous lipid microenvironments. While an n-6-enriched diet accelerated PDAC growth, an n-3-enriched diet suppressed tumor growth in a T cell-independent manner. Examining inflammatory effects in PDAC tumors, the n-3 PUFA-enriched diet reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines, including IL-6 family members, and single-cell and spatial analyses identified tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as the primary diet-responsive population. Indeed, selective conversion of n-6 to n-3 fatty acids within myeloid cells using an inducible fat-1 transgene, which encodes an n-3 desaturase that converts n-6 to n-3 PUFAs in vivo, was sufficient to suppress tumor growth, whereas fibroblast-restricted conversion had no effect. This finding is the first to formally establish that cellular origin of PUFA metabolism within the TME is a key determinant of tumor progression and identifies TAMs as critical mediators of n-3-dependent tumor suppression. Furthermore, the n-3 PUFA-enriched diet reduced Arg1+ immunosuppressive TAMs and promoted C1q+ and MHC-II+ antigen-presenting TAM populations enriched for antigen processing machinery and T cell-recruiting chemokines, alongside reduced IL-6 family cytokine production. Together, these findings establish macrophages as key mediators of n-3-driven tumor control and define a mechanism by which dietary lipids remodel cytokine signaling in the PDAC microenvironment.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: The basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are not fractal.
abstract: The energy landscape picture is a central tool to study many-body systems. In particular, the energy landscapes of glass-forming liquids, jammed packings, constraint satisfaction problems, or neural networks contain a plethora of minima corresponding to competing states. Due to their complexity, these landscapes resist analytical treatment and must be studied numerically. We focus on jammed soft spheres, a paradigmatic model of glasses and granulars, to expose the limitations of standard numerical methods in resolving the true structure of energy landscapes. We show that the C-language Variable-coefficients ordinary differential equation solver is the one with the best time-for-error trade-off for this problem, outperforming commonly used steepest-descent solvers by several orders of magnitude. Using this numerical approach, we provide unequivocal evidence that optimizers widely used in computational studies destroy all semblance of the true landscape geometry, even in moderately low dimensions. Employing a range of geometric indicators, both low- and high-dimensional, we show that earlier claims on the fractality of basins of attraction of minima originated from the use of inadequate mapping strategies. In reality, the basins of attraction of soft-sphere packings are smooth structures with well-defined length scales, a result that likely extends to a much broader family of problems.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Reconstructing actin dynamics of the leading edge from observational data.
abstract: Mesenchymal cell migration starts with the protrusion of the cell's leading edge, enabled by the branching growth of the actin network. Two crucial molecular players in protrusion are actin filaments and the Arp2/3 complex, the branching agent. Traditionally, protrusion models are intuited from several perturbative experiments. Recent multiplex microscopy imaging data promise to change this paradigm by providing measurements of naturally fluctuating densities of key proteins at the leading edge of unperturbed cells. We report an attempt to reconstruct the mechanistic protrusion model from such data. We analyze fluctuations of densities of actin filaments and Arp2/3 complex and cell edge velocity using phase space and regression analysis to reconstruct linearized dynamics of the coupled actin-Arp2/3-velocity system. We then build a nonlinear model of these dynamics based on previous knowledge of this system and parsimony. The resulting models recover the rates of reactions and mechanical and transport processes in the lamellipodium from a single nonperturbative experiment. The models posit that the dominant nonlinear term in the lamellipodial dynamics corresponds to the retrograde flow of the actin network in the cell frame. The models suggest that the protrusion is dominated by a damped oscillatory cycle resulting from a combination of positive feedback from the Arp2/3 complex to protrusion velocity and negative feedback from actin density to the velocity.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: In vivo virus-free lineage tracing and live imaging reveal that NeuroD1 does not reprogram microglia into neurons.
abstract: In situ glia-to-neuron conversion induced by a single transcription factor is a promising regenerative strategy for treating central nervous system injuries and neurodegenerative diseases. Previous studies reported that NeuroD1 can induce microglia-to-neuron cross-lineage conversion and improve recovery after brain injury. However, these findings remain controversial. To examine the ability of NeuroD1 in inducing microglia-to-neuron conversion, we employed virus-free genetic lineage-tracing systems in mice to specifically induce NeuroD1 expression in microglia and track the cell fate of NeuroD1-expressing cells at multiple timepoints. Meanwhile, we longitudinally monitored NeuroD1-expressing microglia via two-photon imaging and characterized their transcriptional profile by single-cell RNA sequencing. All observations across these methods revealed that NeuroD1-expressing cells retained their microglia identity and cannot convert into neurons, no matter under physiological and injury conditions. Instead, sustained expression of NeuroD1 facilitated microglia apoptosis in vivo. Collectively, our findings provide strong evidence that NeuroD1 alone is not sufficient to induce microglia-to-neuron conversion. This study further highlights the importance of rigorous lineage-tracing and cell fate-mapping strategies for validating in situ glia-to-neuron conversion.

title: RiboTRAP-seq identifies spatially distinct functions for the anterior and posterior intestine in immune and metabolic regulation in Caenorhabditis elegans.
abstract: The intestine integrates food-derived cues to coordinate organismal physiology, yet the molecular specialization of discrete regions along the intestinal epithelium remains unclear. Here, we generate cell type-specific translatomes of the Caenorhabditis elegans intestine during fasting and refeeding using discrete promoters for the anterior quartet of intestinal cells (INT1) and the remaining eight pairs of intestinal cells (INT2-9). We found that the anterior-most INT1 cells are a translationally distinct intestinal subcompartment that is particularly enriched for immune- and stress response genes. Functional assays using novel INT1-specific genes emerging from this study reveal that these specialized cells play a previously unappreciated role in pathogen avoidance and organismal survival. A second critical function of INT1 cells is their role in sensing and responding to the contents of the gut lumen. We show that luminal pyruvate is the key signal linking bacterial nutrients in the gut to secretion of the gut insulin antagonist INS-7. These findings establish INT1 as sentinel enteroendocrine cells that integrate metabolic and immune cues to couple food status with immune and endocrine responses. Our studies also provide a rich resource for dissecting segment-specific intestinal biology, an overlooked and fertile area for future research.

title: Separable downmodulation of meiotic axis protein deposition and DNA break induction at chromosome ends.
abstract: In many organisms, meiotic crossover recombination is suppressed near the extreme ends of chromosomes. Here, we show that multiple, often chromosome-specific, suppressive mechanisms with differing ranges contribute to the consistently low enrichment of recombination-promoting axis proteins and the downregulation of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) within 20 kb of telomeres in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Suppression of axis proteins is associated with cis-encoded signals and correlates with reduced coding density, although whether this sequence feature actively drives suppression remains to be determined. In addition, axis protein suppression requires the histone methyltransferase Dot1 and the Sir silencing complex. We show that Dot1 suppresses Sir complex activity at least in part independently of its canonical target, H3K79, to downmodulate axis protein deposition near chromosome ends. In parallel, the Sir complex, but not Dot1, suppresses the induction of DSBs at a small number of cryptic hotspots by limiting the openness of promoters, the preferred sites of meiotic DSB formation. Much of the reduced DSB induction near chromosome ends persists in dot1 and sir3 mutants, indicating that additional layers of regulation contribute to the robust reduction of meiotic recombination effectors near chromosome ends.

title: Individual dopaminergic neurons induce unique, yet overlapping combinations of behavioural modulations, including safety learning, memory retrieval, and acute locomotion.
abstract: Two evolutionary highly conserved functions of dopamine are to carry 'teaching' signals during associative learning and to control movement. In mammals and humans, these functions are generally thought to be produced by different populations of neurons. Here, we investigated in the larva of Drosophila melanogaster whether both these functions can be induced by the same individual dopaminergic neurons in the central brain. Focusing on the dopaminergic neurons of the DL1 cluster, we asked whether the optogenetic activation of individual neurons established associative punishment and/or safety memories, controlled the retrieval of the established memories, and acutely modulated locomotion. We found that each neuron had a unique yet overlapping set of behavioural effects. Several individual neurons both established a memory and modulated acute locomotion by increasing the animals' bending and decreasing their velocity. Our results demonstrate that individual dopaminergic neurons can fulfil a surprisingly broad range of functions in different behavioural contexts. Given the highly conserved roles of the dopaminergic system across the animal kingdom, this study raises the question whether a similarly diverse functionality can be found also in other animals, including humans.

title: The mechanosensitive channel TMEM63B contributes to noxious heat sensation in the dorsal root ganglia.
abstract: In mammals, heat sensation is primarily mediated by thermosensitive channels, particularly transient receptor potential (TRP) channels, in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons. However, whether additional channels contribute to noxious heat detection remains unclear. Here, we investigated the role of the mechanosensitive cation channel TMEM63B in DRG neurons and unexpectedly discovered its involvement in noxious thermosensation rather than mechanosensation. TMEM63B was broadly expressed in DRG neurons, and its global knockout or DRG-specific conditional knockout markedly reduced heat sensitivity. Deletion of TMEM63B significantly attenuated heat-induced calcium responses and currents in DRG neurons and elevated the temperature threshold for action potential initiation. Recombinant TMEM63B exhibited moderate heat response in calcium imaging assays. Notably, in the presence of arachidonic acid, TMEM63B was strongly activated by heat, suggesting that its thermosensitivity is modulated by the membrane lipid environment. Together, these findings identify TMEM63B as a novel channel contributing to heat sensation and reveal a lipid-dependent modulation of its channel activity.

title: Weak dispersal and landscape size inevitably promote local biodiversity in heterogeneous metacommunities of competing species.
abstract: We provide a general theoretical explanation for a longstanding result in spatial ecology: weak dispersal among habitat patches promotes local species richness. Using analytical approximations of spatial Lotka-Volterra competition models, we show that local species persistence in heterogeneous landscapes can be expressed as the balance between the total density across patches and the local exclusion rate. We further demonstrate that local multispecies coexistence is governed by the feasibility domain, linking spatial coexistence to a structural property of nonspatial competitive systems. Together, these results explain why weak dispersal increases local species richness and why this effect strengthens with the number of available patches, i.e., landscape size. We test these predictions using numerical simulations and find that the theory breaks down only when both dispersal and competitive interactions are very strong, in which case dispersal has a unimodal effect on coexistence. In contrast, landscape size retains a positive effect on coexistence whenever an effect is detectable. We then apply the theory to long-term data from a natural metacommunity of microcrustaceans. We detect strong competition among species and find no detectable effect of dispersal rate on local coexistence, whereas species co-occurrence increases with local landscape size, as predicted by theory. Together, our results identify how dispersal, interaction strength, and landscape size jointly regulate local species richness in competitive systems.

title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug sensitivity measurements into cell subtype- and single-cell-specific profiles. We first validate CLIMB using in-vitro mixtures of leukemic cell lines with experimentally known cell-type proportions, then extend this validation to large-scale, cross-dataset pseudo-bulk analyses built from independent scRNA-seq references across two disease contexts and five cancer types - mimicking the reference-to-target mismatches encountered in real applications - and show that CLIMB accurately infers the cellular composition of bulk samples, outperforming state-of-the-art bulk deconvolution methods. We emphasize CLIMB's effectiveness in acute myeloid leukemia, where it offers highly accurate estimation of leukemic stem cell fractions across three test datasets and three patient cohorts. We then validate CLIFF, our algorithm for estimating cell subtype- and single-cell-specific drug sensitivity, first on the same in-vitro cell line mixtures using experimentally measured drug responses, and then through in-depth, realistic-scale pseudo-bulk simulations. We applied our deconvolution strategy to the beatAML cohort dataset, currently the most extensive database of ex-vivo drug screening data. This analysis generated a cell subtype-resolved drug sensitivity landscape for 121 compounds, revealing multiple compounds putatively active against leukemic stem cells, including midostaurin, A-674563, SNS-032, and foretinib. Collectively, our work introduces a general computational framework for resolving bulk functional measurements at cell-type and single-cell resolution, providing an attractive new computational tool for drug development and precision medicine.

title: Ten simple rules for developing a reporting appraisal tool.
abstract: In an ideal world, authors would report clearly and transparently exactly what they conducted. In reality, reporting is often incomplete, and key elements of research conduct are frequently missing from manuscripts. Reporting guidelines were developed to address this problem by helping authors identify what should be reported. These guidelines have been highly valuable for authors, but they are not well suited for appraising reporting during peer review or editorial assessment despite common use. This is because authors and appraisers have different needs: authors require a comprehensive guide for writing, whereas appraisers need a tool that is concise, repeatable, and easy to use. We therefore propose the development of reporting appraisal tools: operationalised tools designed specifically to assess whether a paper has reported the minimum essential elements of a study. To support their development, we present 10 simple rules.

title: Visual tools for 3D plasma simulation: GPU-based isosurface extraction and particle-based rendering.
abstract: This paper presents a GPU-accelerated visualization framework for interactive exploration of fusion-plasma simulation data represented as scalar fields and particle trajectories. The primary technical contribution is a capacity-safe isosurface-extraction pipeline that combines inclusive slab partitioning with a two-pass counting and exact allocation strategy. This design prevents slab-boundary omissions and output-buffer overflow while supporting large scalar grids. The generated positions and normals are written directly to CUDA-OpenGL interoperable buffers, enabling the standalone renderer to display explicit isosurfaces without an intermediate CPU-side copy. The extracted geometry and scalar-volume data are additionally integrated into Unreal Engine through a separate staging interface. This integration provides a unified environment for volume rendering, explicit-isosurface inspection, particle-trajectory visualization, clipping, and VR-based spatial exploration. These engine-side functions are used as interaction and visualization mechanisms rather than being presented as new rendering algorithms. Experiments on electromagnetic-potential fields with resolutions up to 5123 demonstrate stable isosurface extraction across different isovalues. In the most geometrically complex tested case, the method generates approximately 42.81 million vertices in 44.7 ms, uses less than 11 GB of GPU memory, and renders the resulting geometry at 28.6 FPS. The results indicate that the proposed framework provides a practical explicit-surface visualization path for large plasma datasets while complementing direct volume rendering and established scientific-visualization toolkits.

title: Metaphor, multimodality and generative AI: Synthetic images prompted by figurative expressions in anti-immigration discourse.
abstract: Complex social processes like migration are frequently understood via metaphors. In right-wing media and far-right political discourses, two metaphors that abound draw on flood and invasion frames to problematise immigration and legitimise hostile attitudes and actions towards it. In so far as metaphor involves the construction of mental imagery, it is intimately bound with visual experience, including semiotically mediated visual experience. In a semiotic landscape increasingly populated by synthetic images, I argue that the meaning of metaphors may be modulated by AI-generated visual content and that this is especially important in contexts of political communication. The study investigates images generated by prompts instantiating an immigration is flood versus an immigration is invasion metaphor to inquire if and how they differ by source-frame and what are the ideological implications of the images returned. Following an initial pilot study, several specific semiotic features are analysed, including colour, properties of the figure (size, shape, orientation) and ground elements (environment, securitising features and frame-consistent features like fire and water). Results show significant differences between metaphorical frames and highlight the potential that AI-generated images have to reflect and reinforce ideological positions.

title: Quantifying the diagnostic time gap in precision oncology: A retrospective analysis of potential time savings from same-day cartridge-based molecular testing versus next-generation sequencing in cytology specimens.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) turnaround times (TAT) exceed two weeks and can delay the initiation of targeted therapy. Rapid cartridge-based platforms such as Idylla deliver single-gene or fusion results from minimal cytology material within hours, but time savings have not been systematically quantified. METHODS: Forty-two cases of non-small cell lung carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, melanoma, and mammary analogue secretory carcinoma of the salivary gland that underwent both Idylla testing (KRAS, EGFR, BRAF, and GeneFusion assays) and orthogonal NGS at a single academic center were reviewed. NGS TAT was calculated from specimen collection to report release, and Idylla results were modeled as available one day after collection. The primary outcome was per-case time savings (NGS TAT minus one day); treatment timelines were reconstructed from the medical record. Analyses were descriptive; no inferential testing was performed. A sensitivity analysis varied the modeled Idylla TAT from 1 to 3 days, and an adjusted estimate assigned no time saving to the two cartridge results that were not actionable on the day of collection. RESULTS: The median NGS TAT across all 42 cases was 20.0 days (IQR, 17.0-23.8; range, 8-51). Against the modeled 1-day Idylla TAT, the median time savings was 19.0 days per case (IQR, 16.0-22.8; range, 7-50), totaling 858 patient-days. Assigning no time saving to those two cases gave a median of 18.0 days and 817 patient-days. No patient received therapy that was subsequently contradicted by the sequencing result. In thirteen patients, the sequencing interval alone exceeded three weeks, and in seven, no systemic therapy was underway while the result was awaited. CONCLUSIONS: Same-day cartridge-based testing from cytology and small biopsy specimens could provide actionable results a median of 19 days earlier than standard NGS. Whether this translates into earlier treatment initiation was not assessed and requires prospective evaluation.

title: H-HQNN: Hybrid quantum-classical neural network with feature selection by heuristics to predict heart failure.
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the most dominant cause of mortality across the entire world, claiming 17.9 million lives every year. According to recent trends, the mortality rate as a result of heart failure continues to increase particularly in low- and middle-income areas which means that early diagnostic tools desperately need to be discovered. Conventional biomarkers like NT-proBNP, troponins and creatinine levels are useful, although their sensitivity and specificity are low, particularly in identifying heart failure onset before it is actually clinically apparent. We suggest addressing these issues by proposing the following Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Heuristics-Based Feature Selection that can be used to predict the onset of heart failure: H-HQNN: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Heuristics-Based Feature Selection. Given this, SMOTE is used to balance the clinical data and reduce class imbalance, whereas the most informative cardiac biomarkers and clinical features are selected using a two-stage process in which Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) first prunes redundant attributes, followed by a dual-phase optimization where PSO refines the feature subset and Cuckoo Search (CS) enhances global exploration to avoid local minima, resulting in a compact and highly relevant feature set. These features are then represented in a variational quantum circuit (4 qubits) and are implemented as ZZFeatureMap, Pauli-Z gates, EfficientSU2, and RealAmplitudes, which are combined in a hybrid quantum-classical neural network. Performance was estimated using stratified 5-fold cross-validation on a single public dataset; external validation on independent cohorts has not yet been performed. The average accuracy of our model is 96.62% ± 3.45 with precision of 96.11, recall of 96.10, F1-score of 96.54 and AUC = 0.9604. The most efficient fold has 98.30% accuracy and AUC = 0.9872 with a confusion matrix of almost perfect balance in true positive and true negative rates. H-HQNN is more efficient and interpretable as it achieves better discriminative power, with fewer features, compared to classical baselines (e.g., Random Forests, deep neural networks). H-HQNN presents an opportunity toward novel methodology of identifying early heart failure by utilizing quantum-classical hybrid modeling and heuristic feature selection to ensure progress in preventative cardiology and therapeutic intervention in particular where advanced imaging studies or invasive measurements of biomarkers are not feasible.

title: The hidden challenges of return migration: Linguistic and academic re-adaptation of Syrian students to the Arabic Education System.
abstract: While extensive research has examined refugee students' educational adaptation in host countries, the educational reintegration phase following voluntary return remains underexplored. This qualitative study investigates the linguistic and academic adaptation experiences of Syrian students transitioning from Turkish-medium education in Türkiye to Arabic-medium schooling in Syria after voluntary return. The study addresses an overarching question: how do returnee students experience the linguistic, academic, social, and psychosocial dimensions of this reverse educational transition? Using an exploratory qualitative design, data were collected through a seven-item open-ended written questionnaire from 15 middle-school students who had received several years of formal schooling in Türkiye. Qualitative content analysis revealed that return does not constitute a simple linguistic recovery, but rather a reverse academic transition characterized by profound difficulties with academic Arabic, conceptual transfer, written production, and in-class assessment practices. The findings indicate that students' challenges were shaped not only by uneven Arabic literacy development but also by curriculum misalignment, pedagogical practices that participants perceived as more teacher-directed, limited peer interaction, and assessment practices that they perceived as unclear. Furthermore, psychosocial pressures, including re-migration-related distress, concentration difficulties, and increased family responsibilities, complicated their academic adaptation. Ultimately, these struggles reflect systemic institutional and contextual mismatches rather than individual deficits. By conceptualizing return as a distinct educational phase, this study contributes to the broader discourses on refugee education and bilingualism. The implications underscore the critical need for academic Arabic bridging programs, background-sensitive assessment frameworks, psychosocially responsive pedagogies, and school-based psychosocial support to ensure equitable reintegration into Arabic-medium schooling.

title: Identification of SGK1 as a candidate regulator associated with myeloid cell senescence in ME/CFS: An integrative transcriptomic and experimental study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex illness lacking objective diagnostic biomarkers and clear pathophysiological understanding. Patients exhibit immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation reminiscent of aging phenotypes, yet the role of myeloid cell senescence in this disease remains unexplored. METHODS: A stepwise integrative transcriptomic and computational strategy was employed. Differentially expressed genes were identified from the bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE14577. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis was performed to identify key modules correlated with the ME/CFS phenotype. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting these modules with aging-related genes from the GenAge database. Core hub genes were further selected using LASSO regression and random forest machine learning algorithms. Cell type-specific expression was mapped using single-cell RNA sequencing data GSE214283, and functional validation was conducted via siRNA knockdown in a THP-1 cell senescence model. RESULTS: Integrative analysis identified HMGCR and SGK1 as core hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that candidate genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular senescence and inflammation. Single-cell transcriptomics analysis suggested that SGK1 expression was enriched in myeloid cell populations, including monocytes and neutrophils, in individuals with ME/CFS, whereas HMGCR showed a broader expression pattern. Single-gene GSEA indicated that SGK1 was associated with autophagy and lysosomal function. In vitro experiments showed that SGK1 expression was significantly upregulated in D-galactose-induced senescent THP-1 cells, and SGK1 knockdown markedly reduced the mRNA expression levels of senescence markers p16, p21, and p53. CONCLUSION: This study identifies SGK1 as a candidate molecule associated with myeloid cell senescence-related alterations in ME/CFS. Integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses suggest a potential link between SGK1 expression and aging-associated immune alterations. However, further validation in primary ME/CFS-derived immune cells and clinical cohorts is required to determine the biological significance and clinical relevance of SGK1.

title: Meta reinforcement learning for robust quadruped locomotion under joint failures.
abstract: Joint failures can disrupt gait coordination, velocity tracking, and body stability in quadruped robots by reducing the available control authority. This study investigates faults in which joints remain locked at fixed angles and presents Adjudicate Reconfiguration and Evolving Regularization Meta Reinforcement Learning (ARER-MetaRL). The framework combines task inference from context, modular routing tailored to each task through an Adjudicate Reconfiguration (AR) network, and Evolving Gradient Regularization (ER) to support rapid adaptation. Tasks differ in the identities and locking angles of the faulty joints, the number of simultaneous faults, the commanded motion direction, and the terrain. Experiments in NVIDIA Isaac Sim cover all 12 actuated joints, with 0-3 stuck joints during meta-training and severity tests involving up to 6 simultaneously stuck joints. ARER-MetaRL achieves higher Mean Episode Linear Velocity Tracking Reward (MELV) and Mean Episode Roll-Pitch Tracking Reward (MERP) than single-task reinforcement learning, ablated variants, and the evaluated learning and adaptation baselines. Cumulative rewards further demonstrate the benefit of combining the proposed components. In the study of fault severity, ARER-MetaRL achieves MELV/MERP values of 0.86/0.84 with one stuck joint and 0.55/0.54 with six stuck joints, compared with 0.21/0.18 and 0.05/0.03, respectively, for the single-task baseline. These results show improved adaptation across different configurations of locked joints and terrain conditions.

title: A mild, effective, and green micro-dissolution treatment for wool fiber using choline-ascorbic acid NADES.
abstract: Herein, we proposed a mild and effective approach for the surface modification of wool fiber using a natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES) composed of choline chloride and ascorbic acid (Vitamin C), avoiding the unsustainability of oxidation methods and severe damage of enzyme methods. The results showed that the NADES could remove keratin-associated proteins partly due to the breakage of disulfide bonds with the retention of the protein's main macromolecular skeleton and secondary structure, and the exposure degree increase of hydrophilic groups. Furthermore, the hydrophily, dye performance, and anti-felting properties were improved and met industrial standards. The developed method had apparent advances in treatment time, energy consumption, and chemical usage compared to present methods. This work contributes to the further investigation of NADES on the protein modification.

title: Age-stratified prevalence and associated risk factors of hypertension, diabetes and hypercholesterolemia in Nepal: Insights from the STEPS survey 2019.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a major global public health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries such as Nepal. Despite the growing burden of hypertension, diabetes, and hypercholesterolemia, limited evidence exists on age-stratified patterns of NCDs and associated risk factors, especially among younger populations. This study investigated age-stratified prevalence of hypertension, diabetes and hypercholesterolemia and risk factors in Nepal to inform age-specific preventions and policy interventions. METHODS: We analyzed nationally representative data from the 2019 STEPS Survey, including 3,219 participants aged 15-69 years. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests describe participant characteristics. Multivariable logistic regression assessed associations between risk factors and NCDs, while univariate logistic regression, Wilcoxon scores, and pairwise multiple comparisons examined age-group differences in prevalence of NCDs and risk factors. RESULTS: The mean participant age was 35.3 ± 12.8 years, with 56% female. Among adults aged ≥60 years, 50% used tobacco and 31.5% consumed alcohol. Alcohol consumption was also notably prevalent among individuals aged 15-29 years, affecting 30.7% of this age group. Physical inactivity was identified in 18.9% of the overall study population. The highest rates of overweight (30.2%) and stress (80.1%) were among adults aged 30-44, with obesity (9.0%) peaking at 45-59 years. Men (OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.62-2.55) and those aged 60 years or older (OR 4.92, 95% CI 3.35-7.22) had higher odds of hypertension. Diabetes (OR 6.34, 95% CI 3.58-11.23) and hypercholesterolemia (OR 2.66, 95% CI 1.77-3.98) were most prevalent in the 45-59 age group. CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of NCDs and risk factors increases with age, yet substantial burdens exist among younger adults. Age-specific targeted policies should promote healthy behaviors and routine screening in youth, emphasize metabolic risk management and early detection in middle age, and ensure sustained treatment access and continuity of care for older adults.

title: Predictive-feedforward energy management for a hybrid agricultural machine operating in mountainous orchards.
abstract: Hybrid agricultural machines in mountainous orchards operate under low-speed, high-load conditions with coupled gradient and time-varying rolling-resistance disturbances. Their power demand is therefore nonstationary and may change abruptly. Rule-based and instantaneous strategies provide limited preview, whereas model predictive control (MPC) can transmit prediction errors directly to actuator commands and imposes substantial online computation. To address these limitations, a forward model was developed for a power-split hybrid agricultural machine comprising an engine, two electric machines, a traction battery, and a planetary gear set. A predictive-feedforward, multi-objective energy-management strategy was proposed. Short-horizon speed and gradient predictions are normalized, weighted, and saturated to form a bounded load-risk indicator. Rather than entering low-level torque calculation directly, this indicator modifies the dynamic state-of-charge (SOC) safety boundary, power-source mode, and transmission-ratio switching threshold, thereby softly decoupling prediction and execution. Engine high-efficiency operation, two transmission ratios, and actuator constraints are then coordinated for computationally efficient online power allocation. With offline dynamic programming (DP) as a common benchmark, the strategy achieved 93.29-95.59% of the DP performance over cycles C1-C3, exceeding MPC by 1.41-3.19 percentage points and adaptive equivalent-consumption minimization by 3.62-4.99 percentage points. Mean execution time was 0.128-0.191 ms per step, 93.54% lower than that of MPC, while terminal SOC remained near 0.600. No SOC, battery-current, or power-source torque constraint was violated under prediction noise or abrupt equivalent rolling-resistance disturbances. The conclusions apply to maintained, firm orchard lanes with low track slip; soft-soil operation involving high traction, severe sinkage, or substantial slip requires further validation. Bounded load-risk feedforward thus retained short-horizon preview while limiting direct error propagation, providing a practical real-time approach for hybrid agricultural machines with resource-constrained embedded controllers.

title: Word-color association from large-scale online data: Methodology and applications.
abstract: Words and colors are intimately associated in humans, a sign of the close relationship between verbal, linguistic expression and cognition. Word-color association therefore plays an important role in areas of communication such as marketing and literature. Traditional efforts to build a general, scalable, and quantitative mapping of word-color association have often relied on surveys, experiencing difficulties in curating large-scale data sets, enrolling sufficient participants, and excising potential inherent researcher biases in the choice of the words and the colors to be mapped. Even the most recent computational efforts based on Large Language Models (LLMs) do not overcome these problems due to their near-complete lack of transparency in data and methodology that results in low confidence, consistency, and reliability. Here we propose a framework that overcomes these limitations via the use of freely accessible large-scale web image data, and fully transparent and reproducible methods that allow one to build color associations for almost any given word. We also showcase the methodology in action through analyses of color usage in corporate branding and 20th-century Anglo-American poetry. These show that our framework can help form new answers to and perspectives on long-standing questions in communication. Additionally, our framework by design can be readily adopted for use in any language supported by a web image search engine, and its code is freely available in open source; we therefore expect it to contribute towards achieving a universal, multilingual understanding of word-color association.

title: Identifying diagnostic testing gaps for antiphospholipid syndrome within a single healthcare system.
abstract: Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS) is a rare disease with significant morbidity and the possibility of mortality. While there are no established diagnostic criteria for use in clinical settings, there is a large body of global research organized by the American College of Rheumatology and European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (ACR/EULAR) into accepted research guidelines, developed for identifying probable APS cases. The research guidelines were used in this study as a surrogate approach for evaluating diagnostic testing patterns, with the aim of identifying potential gaps in patient evaluation for APS in clinical settings. For this study, suggested testing for APS characterization included IgG (Immunoglobulin G) and IgM (Immunoglobulin M) anti-cardiolipin antibodies; IgG and IgM anti-beta-2 glycoprotein I antibodies; and Lupus Anticoagulant. This retrospective cross-sectional study identified patients from the electronic medical records of a regional health system with International Classification of Diseases (ICD) diagnostic codes for APS-associated conditions, signs, symptoms, and/or testing collected for antiphospholipid antibodies in selected medical and surgical specialty locations, from 01/01/2011 to 12/31/2020. These data were used to assess how closely the clinical testing patterns followed the 2023 ACR/EULAR criteria for laboratory evaluation. The data showed that 80.70% of 16679 patients with antiphospholipid antibody tests collected did not include all antiphospholipid antibody testing described in 2023 ACR/EULAR research criteria guidelines. These findings may represent common suboptimal ordering practices in evaluations for APS, highlighting the need for peer comparison and the development of future clinical laboratory guidance to support more complete assessment for APS.

title: Perceived AIGC saturation and AI content fatigue on short-video platforms: An appraisal-based structural equation modeling study.
abstract: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is increasingly embedded in short-video platforms, where algorithmic recommendation systems expose users to high volumes of rapidly produced synthetic media. Although prior research has examined generative AI from the perspectives of creativity, productivity, and technology adoption, less is known about how ordinary users evaluate repeated exposure to AI-generated short videos. This study develops and tests an appraisal-based model of AI content fatigue, distinguishing perceived AIGC saturation from users' appraisals of low-quality prevalence, narrative homogenization, and content overload. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Chinese short-video users in May 2026. After excluding invalid responses, 513 valid questionnaires were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling. The adjusted structural model showed acceptable fit to the data, χ²(1321) = 1991.541, χ²/df = 1.508, CFI = .946, TLI = .929, IFI = .947, and RMSEA = .031. Perceived AIGC saturation was positively associated with perceived low-quality prevalence, perceived narrative homogenization, and perceived content overload. Perceived low-quality prevalence had the largest estimated coefficient, followed by perceived content overload, whereas perceived narrative homogenization was not supported under bootstrap inference. AI content fatigue was negatively associated with satisfaction and continued viewing intention. Bootstrap analyses indicated selected path-specific indirect associations from perceived AIGC saturation to AI content fatigue, satisfaction, and continued viewing intention. Indirect pathways through perceived low-quality prevalence and perceived content overload were supported, whereas those through perceived narrative homogenization were not. The findings indicate that fatigue in AIGC-rich short-video environments is not simply a response to AI-generated content itself. It is more closely related to users' appraisals of content quality, repetitiveness, and cognitive burden. The study contributes to social media fatigue research by conceptualizing AI content fatigue as a content-specific evaluative state and offers implications for platform governance, AIGC labeling, recommendation diversity, and quality-sensitive moderation.

title: Rates of nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) regression among patients with very mild or mild NPDR in an Indian Health Service teleophthalmology program, 2015 - 2020.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) regression is not regularly reported; yet understanding of its prevalence in early-stage DR may impact strategies for eye care management. This study's primary aim was to examine DR regression in patients initially diagnosed with very mild or mild nonproliferative DR (NPDR). A secondary aim was to assess the association between retinopathy regression and diabetes therapy, diabetes duration, and Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c). This was a retrospective, longitudinal cohort study using medical record data from the United States's Indian Health Service's teleophthalmology program for DR evaluation. Baseline exams occurred in 2015-2017 and follow-up (FU) exams occurred within 3 years of baseline. There were 2,348 patients included in this cohort with very mild NPDR at baseline and 705 patients with mild NPDR. For the whole sample, mean age was 56 ± 12.8 years, 55% were female, diabetes duration was 13.0 ± 9.1 years, and HbA1c was 8.8 ± 2.1%. Proportions for DR regression were 0.47 (CI = .45 - .50) (from very mild NPDR) and 0.36 (CI = 0.33-0.40) (from mild NPDR). Proportions for any DR progression were 0.27 (CI = 0.25-0.29) (from very mild NPDR) and 0.34 (CI = 0.30-0.38) (from mild NPDR). Multivariable analyses showed that lower HbA1c levels were associated with greater odds of diabetic retinopathy regression in patients with either very mild or mild baseline NPDR, whereas insulin use was associated with lower odds of regression. Shorter diabetes duration was associated with greater odds of regression only among patients with very mild NPDR at baseline. DR regression was more frequent than DR progression particularly for patients initially with very mild NPDR. DR reversal was more likely in early-stage DR. Behavioral modifications such as increased physical activity and weight loss that lower HbA1c and subsequent risks for DR progression are important to emphasize in diabetic eye care.

title: Bridging material culture networks and social networks in archaeology.
abstract: This study examines whether material culture can serve as a proxy for past social interaction. Using the ArchMatNet agent-based model, we simulate social behavior in small-scale communities and resulting material culture production, then compare social and material culture networks. We compare networks using graph correlation and the quadratic assignment procedure, evaluate parameter effects with generalized additive models, and assess underlying structures with exponential random graph models. Within this simulated system, results show strong correlations between social interaction networks and material culture networks, especially when material culture traits are sufficiently variable. However, correlations weaken under some conditions, particularly low material culture variation, indicating limits to archaeological network inference. Key factors include interaction frequency, learning strategy, and trait visibility. These results characterize hypothetical relationships generated under the model's assumptions; they do not constitute empirical validation. They highlight both the promise and the constraints of using material culture as a proxy for social networks and underscore the need for empirical testing and careful attention to network structure.

title: BTSR-Net: Boundary-topology guided structural refinement for high-resolution remote sensing image segmentation.
abstract: Semantic segmentation of high-resolution remote sensing imagery in complex urban scenes often suffers from insufficient modeling of boundary neighborhoods, causing ambiguity near class interfaces and weakening the continuity of elongated structures. To address this issue, we propose a Boundary-Topology-Guided Structural Refinement Network (BTSR-Net). Built upon HRNet-OCR, BTSR-Net introduces a Geometric Boundary-Distance Branch (GBD) with joint boundary-distance supervision to capture spatial transitions around class boundaries, a Multi-scale Topology-Guided Structural Fusion (MTSF) module to enhance connectivity representation of elongated structures, and a dual-stream structural refinement mechanism to perform local residual correction within a boundary-distance-defined refinement narrow-band. Experiments on the ISPRS Potsdam and Vaihingen datasets demonstrate improvements in overall segmentation accuracy, boundary quality, and structural connectivity. On Potsdam, BTSR-Net achieves 84.70% mIoU, 43.17% mBIoU, and 81.63% clDice, exceeding the baseline by 2.91, 5.66, and 3.74 percentage points, respectively. On Vaihingen, it achieves 93.94% mIoU, 73.90% mBIoU, and 95.46% clDice, with corresponding improvements of 2.27, 9.39, and 2.12 percentage points. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of BTSR-Net for structure-sensitive semantic segmentation in high-resolution remote sensing imagery.

title: A retrospective epidemiological study of screening-derived solid cancer incidence proxy rates in South Korea before and after COVID-19 using Korean National Health Insurance Service data.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted cancer screening and diagnostic pathways globally. Aggregate screening-derived indicators require cautious interpretation because they do not represent confirmed cancer registry incidence but might reflect program participation, referral patterns, and denominator composition. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate pre- and post-COVID-19 changes in selected solid cancer screening-derived incidence proxy rates in South Korea, and to estimate model-based proxy rates through 2028. METHODS: This retrospective ecological longitudinal study analyzed publicly available aggregate annual cancer-screening statistics from the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) and Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) for six solid cancer programs (stomach, liver, colorectal, breast, cervical, and lung cancer). Annual proxy rates per 100,000 screened or eligible persons were calculated. Pre-COVID (2010-2019) and post-COVID (2020-2024) means were compared using Welch t-tests with Mann-Whitney U sensitivity analyses. Ordinary least-squares (OLS) forecasts were generated for 2025-2028. Interrupted time-series analysis was not feasible owing to an insufficient post-COVID observation window. RESULTS: Post-COVID changes in proxy rates were heterogeneous across selected programs. Breast cancer proxy rates increased by 17.1% (Welch p = 0.002) and liver cancer proxy rates by 83.6% (Welch p = 0.002); the liver cancer increase reflects denominator restriction to a high-risk population rather than a true epidemiological surge. Stomach cancer decreased by 23.3% (Welch p = 0.001), cervical cancer by 56.9% (Welch p = 0.005), and colorectal cancer by 25.8% (Welch p = 0.007). Lung cancer data were available only from 2019 to 2024 (program inception) and were interpreted descriptively. CONCLUSIONS: Aggregate South Korean national screening data show pandemic-era temporal associations with heterogeneous changes in selected solid cancer program proxy rates. These findings support an indirect screening-disruption and ascertainment interpretation rather than causal proof of a direct COVID-19 effect on solid cancer incidence.

title: SportRGDET: Scene prior and relation graph enhanced detection transformer for sports scenes.
abstract: Object detection in sports videos holds significant application value in tactical analysis, athlete tracking, and intelligent broadcasting. However, existing methods face two key challenges when processing sports scenes: on one hand, target distribution in sports footage is strictly constrained by field boundaries, yet generic detectors uniformly allocate detection resources across the entire image, causing frequent false detections in off-field regions due to the visual similarity between spectators and athletes; on the other hand, objects such as athletes, balls, and referees in sports scenes form stable spatial co-occurrence patterns governed by game rules, yet existing methods predict each object independently, failing to leverage cross-category relational cues to assist the detection of difficult targets. To address these issues, this paper proposes SportRGDET (Sport Relation-Graph DEtection Transformer), a framework that achieves accurate detection through two core modules: the Scene Prior Guided Module (SPGM) jointly estimates the spatial probability distribution and boundary gradient map of the field region from multi-scale encoder features, fuses them to generate a hierarchical field confidence mask, and performs spatial modulation on the deformable self-attention weights of the encoder, which reallocates attention resources toward the effective field area and progressively suppresses off-field interference across layers, thereby reducing false detections while incurring only moderate additional computation; the Relation Reasoning Enhancement Module (RREM) treats each candidate object as a node during the detection decoding stage, adaptively learns inter-node association strengths through a relation encoder based on category embeddings and relative spatial positions of node pairs, constructs a dynamic relation graph, and bidirectionally propagates contextual information across nodes via graph attention mechanisms, enabling difficult targets to refine their predictions by leveraging positional and categorical cues from surrounding identified objects, enhancing detection robustness under occlusion and blur conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that SportRGDET achieves significant performance improvements on multiple sports detection benchmark datasets, validating the effectiveness of scene prior and relation reasoning mechanisms in sports scene object detection.

title: Reliability and validity of the Japanese version of the Sleep Problem Acceptance Questionnaire.
abstract: This study aimed to develop a Japanese version of the Sleep Problem Acceptance Questionnaire (SPAQ-J) and assess its reliability and validity. The SPAQ-J was developed through a forward-backward translation procedure with permission from the original authors. The sample included 861 adults with insomnia who completed questionnaires on experiential avoidance, insomnia symptoms, dysfunctional beliefs about sleep, sleep-related safety behaviors, insomnia catastrophizing, and pre-sleep arousal. Confirmatory factor analysis confirmed that the SPAQ-J retained the two-factor structure of the original version (CFI = 0.972, TLI = 0.958, RMSEA = 0.082, SRMR = 0.059): Activity Engagement and Willingness. Although internal consistency was adequate (Activity Engagement: α = 0.868, ω = 0.870; Willingness: α = 0.895, ω = 0.895), test-retest reliability was below the recommended threshold (Activity Engagement: ICC = 0.586, Willingness: ICC = 0.589). In terms of construct validity, Willingness moderately correlated with all scales, whereas Activity Engagement showed moderate-to-weak correlations. Hierarchical multiple regression analysis revealed that adding the SPAQ-J subscales significantly enhanced the explanatory power. Measurement invariance analysis across sex and age groups showed no significant changes in the fit indices, indicating stability. These findings suggest that the SPAQ-J is a valid and partially reliable measure of psychological flexibility related to sleep problems in the Japanese population.

title: Relation-aware dynamic knowledge subgraph enhanced large language models for medical multiple-choice question answering.
abstract: Medical multiple-choice question answering requires models to simultaneously understand question semantics, candidate-answer differences, and structured relations among medical entities in complex clinical contexts. To address the limitations that existing knowledge-enhanced methods often adopt question-level unified modeling and thus struggle to characterize local relational differences among different candidate options, while conventional low-rank adaptation lacks relation-pattern adaptivity, this paper proposes a knowledge-enhanced large language model framework that combines option-level knowledge subgraph representation fusion with relation-aware dynamic LoRA adaptation. The proposed method first constructs a local medical knowledge subgraph for the question stem and each candidate answer separately, and then injects structured knowledge into candidate representations through a graph encoder and gated fusion mechanism. Subsequently, multiple learned LoRA expert branches are dynamically combined through candidate-conditioned routing based on the relational information encoded in the enhanced candidate representations, enabling the model to obtain more suitable parameter update paths. The experimental results are reported as the mean and standard deviation over three random-seed runs. On the MedQA dataset, the proposed method achieves Accuracy scores of 62.90%±0.82% and 62.84%±1.04%, together with F1-Score values of 62.97%±1.07% and 62.79%±0.78%, using Llama3 8B and Qwen 7B, respectively. On the MedMCQA dataset, the corresponding Accuracy scores are 61.04%±0.30% and 58.59%±0.65%, while the F1-Score values reach 61.21%±0.54% and 57.77%±0.57%, respectively. Experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve knowledge understanding, candidate discrimination, and reasoning stability in medical multiple-choice question answering.

title: The procrastination trap: How temperament undermines students' career readiness in Poland.
abstract: This study examines links between temperament, procrastination tendencies, and self-perceived employability among Polish university students, addressing a notable gap in research on behavioral postponement effects in European higher education contexts. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 522 first-year undergraduates enrolled in 16 fields of study at a mid-sized Polish university. Temperament was assessed with the Formal Characteristics of Behaviour - Temperament Inventory, Revised (FCB-TI(R)); procrastination with the Polish version of Lay's General Procrastination Scale, scored as a single general index; and self-perceived employability with the Polish Self-Perceived Employability Scale (internal and external subscales). Grade point average (GPA) was obtained from university records. Bootstrapped regression-based models estimated the indirect association between each of the seven temperament dimensions and internal employability through procrastination. Procrastination was associated with lower briskness, rhythmicity, sensory sensitivity, endurance and activity, and with higher emotional reactivity and perseveration. For all seven dimensions the indirect association with internal employability through procrastination was significant, with completely standardised indirect effects between  .02 and  .05; for endurance and rhythmicity the association was indirect only. Procrastination was also associated with lower GPA (r = -.17) and with lower external employability (r = -.18), whereas GPA was unrelated to any employability index. Because the design is cross-sectional and all predictors were measured concurrently, these findings describe patterns of association that are consistent with, but do not establish, a mediating process. The results identify temperamentally patterned procrastination as a modifiable correlate of students' career confidence, and caution against treating academic grades as a proxy for employability readiness.

title: Economic valuation of ecosystem services in agriculture and agroforestry: A meta-analysis.
abstract: The economic valuation of ecosystem services in agriculture and agroforestry is crucial for sustainable development. However, valuation methods vary significantly across contexts. Using the PRISMA framework, we systematically reviewed 146 studies, combined effect sizes through meta-analytic modeling, and conducted spatial autocorrelation analyses to explore geographic patterns. Market price valuation (MPV) and contingent valuation (CVM) are the most used methods in ecosystem service assessments, accounting for 25.8% and 20.8% of studies, respectively. The CVM and life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) approaches play a key role in interdisciplinary research, connecting all ecosystem service categories. Analysis revealed extreme heterogeneity and significant publication bias for cultural (CULT), provisioning (PROV), and regulating (REG) services. Valuation outcomes are strongly influenced by the choice of methods (such as MPV and benefit transfer methods) and unit standardization practices, with effect sizes decreasing when values are standardized to United States dollars per ha per year (USD/ha/year). Spatial autocorrelation was minimal, indicating the importance of local context in the valuation results. Temporal trends indicate episodic changes in the relative effectiveness of valuation approaches. Empirically, MPV showed greater robustness (18%) than CVM, which exhibited greater sensitivity to data constraints (16%). These findings highlight the need to prioritize data quality and context specificity within standardized valuation frameworks to improve policy relevance and comparability in ecosystem service assessments, particularly for underrepresented CULT and supporting (SUP) services.

title: The double-edged sword of human-AI collaboration on design students' competence development: The mediating roles of challenge and hindrance appraisals and the asymmetric moderation of teacher AI leadership.
abstract: The deepening integration of generative AI into design education is driving a paradigm shift in human-computer AI collaboration (HAIC) -from mere tool assistance toward intelligent synergy. However, its dual impact on the competency development of design students and the underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Grounded in the Theory of Stress Appraisal, this study constructs a research model to examine the double-edged sword effect of HAIC on Design Competence (DC), introducing teacher AI Leadership (AIL) as a moderating variable. The aim is to reveal the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions through which HAIC influences DC. Employing a questionnaire survey, this study conducted an empirical investigation involving 483 design students in East China. Data analysis was performed using SPSS 24.0 and Amos 23.0, encompassing reliability and validity tests, regression analysis, and Bootstrap mediation analysis. The results indicate that HAIC influences DC through dual pathways: it positively enhances DC by fostering Challenge Appraisal (CA) (β = 0.283, p < 0.01), which in turn positively predicted competence development (β = 0.363, p < 0.01), yielding a significant indirect effect of 0.103 (p < 0.01). Simultaneously, HAIC triggered Hindrance Appraisal (HA) (β = 0.271, p < 0.01), which negatively predicted competence development (β = -0.229, p < 0.01), yielding a significant indirect effect of -0.062 (p < 0.01). This constitutes a partial mediating mechanism characterized by "one positive, one negative" effect. Furthermore, Teacher AIL exhibits an asymmetric moderating effect: it significantly buffers the positive impact of HAIC on HA (β = -0.112, p < 0.01), indicating that high AIL can mitigate cognitive load and anxiety arising from technological uncertainty, yet it does not significantly amplify the positive pathway via CA (β = 0.001, p > 0.05). The findings suggest that the impact of HAIC on DC is not linear but rather a dialectical process contingent upon individual cognitive appraisal. The core value of Teacher AIL lies in "risk mitigation" rather than "creativity stimulation," offering a theoretical foundation for the intelligent transformation of educational design. At the practical level, it is imperative to facilitate from knowledge deliverers to cognitive facilitators in AI-augmented design education. By systematically developing AI instructional competencies and reforming assessment systems, educators can guide students toward establishing a healthy relationship with HAIC, thereby achieving the synergistic advancement of technological empowerment and humanistic literacy.

title: Disaster-related information support systems for families of older adults with special healthcare needs: A scoping review.
abstract: Based on the theory of structural vulnerability, this study systematically examines the characteristics and underlying mechanisms shaping information needs among families of older adults with special healthcare needs in disaster contexts, providing a theoretical foundation for developing a family-system collaborative disaster information support system. In this scoping review, we systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Data, VIP Database, and the Chinese Biomedical Literature Database from inception to December 31, 2025. A total of 22 studies were included. The findings suggest that the information needs in this population are highly heterogeneous, particularly among families managing cognitive impairments and chronic diseases. These families not only bear the responsibility of information transmission but also act as intermediaries responsible for translating, interpreting, and filtering information. However, existing disaster information support systems insufficiently meet their needs, particularly regarding information accessibility and comprehensibility, which presents significant gaps. Additionally, family caregivers face a disparity between responsibility and capacity, lacking effective support tools, potentially contributing to decision fatigue and information overload. Overall, the study suggests that the information needs of these families may arise from structural mechanisms embedded within disaster response systems. Future disaster information support strategies should move beyond the simple "family-centered" approach to a family-system synergy model. Such an approach should incorporate decision-support toolkits and parallel communication channels while also providing structured decision support and risk-sharing mechanisms. This shift would transform family caregivers from unsupported gap-fillers into active yet supported decision participants, thereby enhancing both disaster response capacity and equity for this vulnerable population.

title: Clustering of patient-derived laboratory data: A privacy-preserving distributed approach to enhance clinical laboratory quality control and regional external quality assessment.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Traditional quality control (QC) has inherent limitations, and there are still various challenges existing in patient-based real-time QC (PBRTQC) and patient-based quality assurance (PBQA). We developed an integrated PBRTQC-PBQA model using density-based clustering and evaluated its effectiveness as a regional clinical laboratory quality assurance tool. METHODS: A 20-month multicentre study across seven hospitals analysed five haematological analytes(white blood cell count [WBC], red blood cell count [RBC], haemoglobin [HGB], platelet count [PLT], and mean corpuscular volume [MCV]). Custom Clustering-PBRTQC-PBQA(CPP) models were developed using log/Box-Cox transformation, 3D spatial construction with companion analytes determined by distribution morphology, Mahalanobis distance filtering (chi-square = 0.3, ~ 47% exclusion rate), and iterative OPTICS clustering to identify hospital-specific core reference populations. A privacy-preserving distributed architecture transmitted only aggregated statistical summaries. Median/EWMA harts (PBRTQC) and Z-score/relative bias charts (PBQA) were created alongside a closed-loop quality improvement system and calibration event verification. RESULTS: The CPP model reduced EWMA alert episodes by 25.0% (92-69) while increasing 1-3S alert episodes by 31.2% (64-84) compared with conventional moving-average PBRTQC, demonstrating selective elimination of systematic bias signals while preserving sensitivity to random errors (net change: 180-173 episodes, -3.9%). Overall calibration consistency was 82.3% (95% CI: 74.1%-88.7%). Among 52 confirmed true-positive alerts, 37 (71.2%) were detected without concurrent internal QC out-of-control signals, demonstrating the model's capacity to capture low-magnitude biases that conventional IQC misses. CONCLUSION: Density-based clustering underpins the PBRTQC-PBQA model's effectiveness in deriving hospital-specific core reference values, filtering unconfirmed QC alerts, validating calibration, and enhancing regional test consistency. The model's ability to detect systematic biases not captured by IQC underscores its value as a complementary quality assurance layer. Its lightweight design supports regional deployment.

title: Self-reported prevalence of tuberculosis and selected associated vulnerability factors among rural populations in six districts of India: A community-based cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis is a major public health challenge in India, contributing to one-fourth of global burden of TB disease. Comorbidities in uninfected individuals make them vulnerable to TB disease. This study estimates the self-reported prevalence of tuberculosis and selected vulnerability factors (HIV, current smoking, silicosis, occupational silica-dust exposure, diabetes mellitus and persistent cough >2 weeks) among the rural demography of six districts in India, with the aim of informing targeted active case finding under the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP). METHODS: The study conducted was a community-based cross-sectional survey carried out across six districts of India. Two blocks from each district was selected randomly followed by randomly selected villages under each block. A universal sampling technique was followed for including all the households of the randomly selected villages. The data were collected through a pre-tested semi-structured questionnaire schedule via face-to-face interviews at all the eligible households of the study sites. Descriptive analysis was performed, and the results were obtained in the form of frequencies and percentages. RESULTS: The ultimate data consisted of 82,636 individuals, with males at 52% and females at 47%. 77% of the study population were 15 years of age or older. This study analyzes a large dataset. The TB prevalence was around 150 per lakh of the population, while the prevalence of HIV-reactive individuals, current smokers, silicosis, occupational exposure to silica dust, diabetes mellitus and cough of greater than two weeks is found in 0.9%, 5%, 1.2%, 1.1%, 1.4% and 4% respectively. DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: The study highlights TB status and selected TB-vulnerable groups. The study has a large sample size, and it follows multipronged approach to study selected vulnerable population groups. This data may improve targeted active case finding among the high-risk groups as outlined by NTEP and provide better TB control strategy outcome at high TB burden settings.

title: Self-perceived competencies of Master of Public Health graduates and recommendations for programs in South Africa.
abstract: The Master of Public Health (MPH) degree is a key qualification for public health practice in low- and middle-income countries. Graduates entering practice should possess a range of competencies to address complex health issues in managerial, technical or research positions. As competencies of graduates exiting South African MPH programs are unknown, a consortium of academics from South African universities conducted an on-line survey of alumni exiting between 2012-2016, to determine their self-reported public health competencies and their recommendations for improving academic programs. Competencies were explored in 11 domains, through three lenses - their reported usefulness at work; perceptions whether they were obtained through MPH programs; and graduates' confidence in their application. Over 80% of this cohort of 221 graduates, mostly in their mid-30's, largely from South Africa and sub-Saharan Africa, needed the competencies in all 11 domains at work, which were felt to be largely obtained from the MPH, and most were confident using them. However, one fifth were not confident in crisis management and 13% were not confident in health promotion. On average 30% reported they did not obtain either crisis management or leadership skills from the MPH. Respondents recommended changes to course content and organization included more experiential learning, mentorship and faculty advocacy for graduate employment. In the absence of country-wide governance for public health education, the study is a first step towards developing core-competencies for South African programs. Findings can be factored into MPH program reviews with attention given to enhancing leadership, crisis management and monitoring and evaluation training into existing courses. Additionally, more experiential learning could fill identified gaps in problem-solving and project management skills. Producing a 'fit for purpose' public health workforce requires alignment of education objectives with health workforce systems in country contexts to ensure a seamless transition between learning and working.

title: The relationship between the use of fillers and Japanese proficiency: Focusing on OPI level assessment.
abstract: This study employed a Cumulative Link Mixed Model (CLMM) to examine the relationship between Japanese learners' filler use and OPI (Oral Proficiency Interview) level ratings. The results showed no significant association with proficiency for the i(い)-group, u(う)-group, ano(あの)-group, and eeto(ええと)-group fillers. In contrast, the a(あ)-group, e(え)-group, o(お)-group, and n(ん)-group fillers were significantly negatively associated with higher proficiency, while the use of maa(まあ)-group and sono(その)-group fillers was significantly positively associated with higher proficiency. Furthermore, an analysis of maa(まあ)-group and sono(その)-group fillers based on their functions and discourse roles showed that turn-internal maa(まあ) and inferential/re-presenting sono(その) require at least two clauses to be produced. This indicates a connection with paragraph-level language production, which is one of the criteria for 'Text Type' in OPI assessment. It was also found that the use of these fillers with such functions is significantly positively associated with higher proficiency. On the other hand, for fillers such as ano(あの) and eeto(ええと), as well as maa(まあ) used in adjacency pairs, no significant increase with proficiency was observed, confirming that their use is not associated with paragraph-level production.
