The use of fillers linked to paragraph-level production can be considered one of the key linguistic factors that can help explain the relationship between filler use and the development of oral language proficiency.

title: Owned dog population profile, dog ownership and bite risk determinants: Key steps to rabies control in Antananarivo, Madagascar.
abstract: Rabies remains a significant public health threat in Madagascar, with dog-mediated transmission causing approximately 1,000 human deaths annually. In Antananarivo, the capital city, control efforts are hindered by limited up to date knowledge on the dog population. This study aims to provide updated estimates of the owned dog population characteristics, identify determinants of ownership, and assess dog bite incidence and risk factors to guide effective vaccination and prevention strategies. Between 2023 and 2025, a longitudinal door‑to‑door household survey was conducted across 21 fokontany (administrative units) in Antananarivo. Of 2,518 surveyed households, 30.5% reported dog ownership, with 1,273 dogs recorded, yielding an estimated dog‑to‑human ratio of 1:9. The owned dog population was predominantly male (63.6%), with a median age of three years. Survival analysis in the selected study site indicated a median lifespan of 4.4 years and an annual mortality hazard of 16%. Vaccination coverage was low: 64.2% of owned dogs had never been vaccinated, primarily due to owners' time constraints, lack of awareness about the need for dog rabies vaccination, and financial barriers. Ownership was positively associated with household location and size, household head's age, education and income. No significant difference in bite risk was observed between dog‑owning and non‑dog‑owning households, whereas households with children under 15 years experienced a significantly higher risk. Rabies elimination among the owned dog population in Antananarivo requires sustained, context‑adapted interventions that address high population turnover. Annual city‑wide dog vaccination campaigns combining door‑to‑door strategies with fixed‑point sites are suggested to increase the chances of reaching a larger share of the owned dog population. Public health efforts must also prioritize paediatric bite prevention and expand access to post‑exposure prophylaxis to contribute to the global goal of eliminating dog‑mediated human rabies by 2030.

title: Laboratory-based surveillance of antimicrobial non-susceptibility in Enterobacter species over 12 years at a tertiary-care hospital in Saudi Arabia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Enterobacter species are increasingly associated with antimicrobial non-susceptibility, but long-term surveillance of temporal trends across antibiotic classes is limited in southern Saudi Arabia. METHODS: We retrospectively studied non-duplicate Enterobacter isolates from adults at a tertiary-care hospital in southern Saudi Arabia (August 2012-August 2024), interpreted by contemporaneous CLSI criteria. Temporal trends were modelled by logistic regression as the annual percent change (APC) in the odds of non-susceptibility, adjusted for care setting, specimen source, age, and sex. Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) and difficult-to-treat resistance (DTR; Kadri criteria) were analysed over time; sensitivity analyses excluded partial years and used breakpoint-comparable periods. RESULTS: Of 1,319 Enterobacter isolates, 91.8% belonged to the Enterobacter cloacae complex. Adjusted trends declined for amikacin (APC -6.1%), gentamicin (-9.4%) and cefepime (-9.1%) and rose for carbapenems (+13.1% to +15.8%), levofloxacin (+6.3%) and piperacillin-tazobactam (+7.0%), with ciprofloxacin stable. The levofloxacin and piperacillin-tazobactam increases did not persist in breakpoint-comparable analyses and are not unequivocal biological increases. Inpatient isolates were more non-susceptible than outpatient isolates by approximately 16-39 percentage points (gentamicin 31.7% vs 14.8%; piperacillin-tazobactam 38.7% vs 23.1%; cefotaxime 63.9% vs 41.5%; cefepime 45.7% vs 28.8%; ceftazidime 61.4% vs 35.3%; ceftriaxone 57.4% vs 18.8%; all p ≤ 0.003). CRE rose early and remained common (APC + 22.8%; 28.7% overall), whereas DTR rose later and stayed infrequent (7.5% of eligible isolates; APC + 16.4%; highest annual value 20.2% in 2023); this difference in timing and overall frequency, not the partially sampled year 2024, indicates dissociation between carbapenem non-susceptibility and loss of all first-line agents. CONCLUSION: Non-susceptibility among Enterobacter species was heterogeneous and antibiotic-specific. The dissociation between CRE and DTR in timing and overall frequency supports using clinically meaningful phenotypes alongside antibiotic-specific trend analysis for stewardship and reporting; the levofloxacin and piperacillin-tazobactam increases warrant caution, as they did not persist in breakpoint-comparable analyses.

title: Medical rehabilitation use and regional bypass among children and adolescents with disabilities: Lessons from South Korea.
abstract: This cross-sectional secondary analysis examined medical rehabilitation use and regional bypass among Korean children and adolescents with registered disabilities, using a two-stage access framework that distinguished entry into medical-institution rehabilitation from out-of-region use after entry. We analyzed public-use data from the 2023 National Survey on Persons with Disabilities, restricting the sample to respondents younger than 19 years (n = 399; weighted national estimate, 88,611). Weighted descriptive statistics and modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors were used to estimate prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Overall, 50.0% had no medical-institution rehabilitation use, 31.5% used in-region rehabilitation, and 18.6% used out-of-region rehabilitation; among rehabilitation users, 37.1% reported out-of-region care. In stage 1, non-developmental disability type was associated with higher medical rehabilitation use (PR, 1.61; 95% CI, 1.28-2.03), whereas eup/myeon residence was associated with lower use (PR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.46-0.94). In stage 2, province residence (PR, 2.13; 95% CI, 1.38-3.27) and non-developmental disability type (PR, 1.74; 95% CI, 1.13-2.69) were associated with out-of-region use, while male sex was associated with lower out-of-region use (PR, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.42-0.92). The most common reason for non-use was use of non-medical facilities (27.4%); better treatment and absence of nearby medical institutions were leading reasons for out-of-region care. Pediatric medical rehabilitation access involves challenges to both non-use and out-of-region use, with implications for local entry support, regional capacity-building, and cross-sector service integration.

title: Joint associations of 2D-3D urban form with land surface temperature along an urban-rural gradient: Implications for sustainable urban planning.
abstract: As fundamental urban units, buildings are closely associated with urban thermal environments, and their morphological attributes are related to spatial variations in thermal conditions. Although significant progress has been made in characterizing building morphology, the relative importance and joint associations between 2D horizontal characteristics and 3D vertical structures in shaping neighborhood-scale thermal environments along urban-rural gradients remain underexplored. This study integrated multi-source remote-sensing data and Geodetector analysis to examine the joint, grid-level associations of 2D and 3D urban-form indicators with land surface temperature (LST) in Hangzhou, China. Multi-temporal LST data from 2000, 2010, 2015, and 2020 were used to characterize the thermal context, whereas the building-morphology data in 2020 supported a cross-sectional spatial association analysis. The results revealed clear spatial variation in the relative explanatory power of morphological indicators. Specifically, 3D building configurations exhibited the greatest explanatory power in the Core Built-up Area, whereas 2D characteristics showed stronger associations with LST in the Suburban Built-up Area. Interactions between 2D and 3D features generally provided greater explanatory power than individual factors, with several factor pairs showing nonlinear enhancement. These findings highlight the value of jointly considering horizontal land-cover patterns and vertical building form when assessing urban thermal environments. By elucidating gradient-specific thermal regulation processes and multidimensional interactions among built-environment features, this study provides a scientific foundation for spatially targeted, climate-responsive heat mitigation strategies and sustainable urban development.

title: Molecular screening of selected RNA viruses in neotropical wild felids of Brazil.
abstract: Astrovirus, cardiovirus and rotavirus are RNA viruses widely distributed among humans, domestic and wild mammals, including felids, occasionally associated with fatal outbreaks and highly resistant to environmental conditions. Despite this, there are no reports of these viruses in New World felids. The aim of this study was to investigate the presence of astrovirus, rotavirus and cardiovirus in non-domestic felids under human care or in the wild, across multiple Brazilian biomes (i.e., Amazon Forest, Atlantic Forest, Caatinga, and Cerrado). Biological samples (e.g., blood, oral and rectal swabs, and frozen tissues) were submitted to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for astrovirus detection and real-time RT-PCR for rotavirus and cardiovirus, followed by sequencing. Fifty wild felids were analyzed, comprising 40 free-ranging and 10 captive animals: 19 ocelots (Leopardus pardalis), 12 pumas (Puma concolor), seven jaguarundis (Herpailurus yagouaroundi), six southern tiger cats (Leopardus guttulus), three margays (Leopardus wiedii) and three jaguars (Panthera onca). An astrovirus was detected in rectal swab of a healthy captive southern tiger cat, while a genotype G3P[3] Rotavirus alphagastroenteritidis (Rotavirus A) was detected in intestine of a roadkill puma. All felid samples were negative for cardiovirus. Morphological analyses of available formalin-fixed tissues of the rotavirus-positive puma were inconclusive due to autolysis. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first molecular detection of astrovirus and rotavirus in Neotropical wild felid species.

title: Impaired erythroid maturation in murine embryos upon loss of the preeclampsia-associated serine protease prostasin Prostasin loss impairs erythropoiesis.
abstract: In humans, the membrane-bound serine protease prostasin encoded by Prss8 is associated with preeclampsia, a gestational hypertension disorder affecting blood supply of the placenta. Deficiency of Prss8 in mice resulted in embryonic lethality by embryonic day (E) 14.5 and impaired maturation of placental labyrinth. We found in Prss8-/- embryos at E11.5 and E12.5 a reduced frequency of both circulating primitive and erythro-myeloid progenitor (EMP)-derived definitive erythroblasts in the yolk sac, placenta and fetal liver. Single-cell RNA sequencing analyses revealed a downregulation of fetal hemoglobin genes and an upregulation of ribosomal genes in primitive erythroid cells of Prss8-/- embryos, indicating a defective erythroid maturation. We suggest that prostasin regulates primitive erythropoiesis in a cell-extrinsic manner, since its expression was absent in circulating erythroid cells. Indeed, the yolk sac vascular remodeling of Prss8-/- embryos was impaired as evidenced by reduced vessel branching and junctions, likely affecting placenta vascularization and contributing to embryonic demise. Our findings unveil a novel role for prostasin during developmental erythropoiesis and vascular patterning and provide insight into how Prss8 dysregulation may contribute to placental pathologies such as preeclampsia.

title: Pain experiences of Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies in China: A descriptive phenomenological study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pain is common in children with hematologic malignancies. It can be highly distressing and can shape how children feel and function during hospitalization. Children's pain experiences are influenced not only by disease and treatment but also by developmental level, family context, language, and culture. However, little is known about how Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies experience and communicate pain in clinical settings. AIM: We aimed to explore the pain experiences of Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies and to inform culturally responsive pain assessment and nursing care. METHODS: We used a descriptive phenomenological design. From February to March 2026, we purposively recruited 15 Tibetan children with hematologic malignancies from a pediatric hematology-oncology ward in Sichuan, China. Data were collected through play-based, semi-structured face-to-face interviews with children and analyzed using an adapted version of Colaizzi's phenomenological method. RESULTS: Four themes were identified: (1) cultural and spiritual interpretations of pain, including silent endurance and religious or traditional coping; (2) linguistic and communicative constraints in pain expression, including limited Mandarin vocabulary and indirect expression of discomfort; (3) family-centered dimensions of pain experience, including emotional security through family presence, relational continuity through family accompaniment, and familiar family-based comfort practices; and (4) hospitalization-related disruptions to everyday social life, including disrupted schooling and peer contact and concerns about illness disclosure and social isolation. CONCLUSIONS: The findings suggest that culturally responsive pain assessment may benefit from child-centered communication, attention to indirect and nonverbal expressions of pain, and recognition of the supportive role of family relationships and familiar comfort practices.

title: Validation of HemoCue method and development of a revised hemoglobin cut-off to detect anemia in children aged 6-24-months.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurate hemoglobin (Hb) measurement is essential for determining anemia prevalence at the population level. The HemoCue method, commonly used in resource poor settings, has been shown to overestimate Hb levels compared to the direct cyanmethemoglobin (DCM) method, leading to an underestimation of anemia. We aimed to validate the HemoCue method against the DCM method and establish an optimal cut-off value for diagnosing anemia in children under two. METHODS: Data were collected from children under two years of age as part of the Etiology, Risk Factors, and Interactions of Enteric Infections and Malnutrition and the Consequences for Child Health and Development study in Bangladesh, conducted in Mirpur, Dhaka, from February 2010 to February 2017. Using HemoCue 201 instrument and DCM method, Hb levels were measured in 846 venous blood samples collected from 589 children. Quadratic regression was explored to derive a correction factor; however, substantial dispersion in HemoCue measurements prevented establishment of a reliable correction model. Youden's Index was used to identify the optimal cut‑off. While it provided a strong threshold, we prioritized achieving at least 70% sensitivity and specificity to confirm balanced diagnostic performance. RESULTS: The median (IQR) Hb concentrations estimated by HemoCue and DCM were 11.6 (10.5, 12.5) g/dL and 10.8 (10.1, 11.5) g/dL, respectively. Using a cut-off of <10.5 g/dL for anemia, the prevalence was significantly higher with the DCM method (35.2% vs. 23.2%, p < 0.001). Considering DCM as the gold standard, the sensitivity and specificity of the HemoCue method were 93% and 53%, respectively. In the test/train analysis, the newly identified cut-off of 11.00 g/dL, indicated an anemia prevalence of 34.2% in the testing dataset, with a sensitivity of 84% and specificity of 69%. CONCLUSION: This study highlights substantial variability between HemoCue and DCM hemoglobin measurements, which prevented development of a reliable correction factor. The proposed HemoCue cut-off of 11.0 g/dL may improve anemia detection in children under two years of age when compared with the currently recommended threshold.

title: Rising stroke burden in Uganda: A national time-series analysis and forecasts, 2016-2028.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability globally, with a disproportionate and growing burden in low- and middle-income Countries. However, evidence on national temporal trends and potential impacts in Uganda remains limited. This study examined trends in stroke cases and deaths in Uganda and forecast of future stroke burden through December 2028. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective time-series analysis of District Health Information System (DHIS2) from 2016 to 2025. Monthly stroke cases, and deaths were analyzed. Monthly populations of Uganda were estimated using exponential growth interpolation and incorporated as an offset term in Bayesian negative binomial regression models to estimate incidence rate ratios (IRR) at 95% confidence interval (CI). Decomposition analysis using the Kitagawa method was applied to derive contributions from population growth and epidemiological change, based on model estimates. Stationarity and autocorrelation were assessed using the unit root and Ljung-Box tests. Forecasting was performed using the exponential smoothing state-space (ETS) model at 80% prediction intervals (PI). RESULTS: Trend analysis showed sustained monthly increases in stroke incidence and mortality with IRR; 1.005 (95% CI: 1.004-1.006), and 1.006 (95% CI: 1.005-1.007), respectively (all p < 0.001). The epidemiological effect was approximately twice as large as the population effect, indicating that the majority of the increase in stroke cases and deaths is attributable to rising incidence rates rather than population growth alone. ETS model demonstrated that by December 2028, monthly cases and deaths are projected to reach approximately 927 (80% PI: 709-1,156) and 126 (80% PI: 94-160), respectively. CONCLUSION: Stroke burden in Uganda is projected to continue increase further over the next years in the absence of effective prevention measures. Strengthened primary prevention, expanded acute stroke care capacity, and improved surveillance systems are urgently needed to mitigate the growing health system impact.

title: Early hospital discharge following delivery during wartime is not associated with increased rates of postpartum hospital referrals.
abstract: BACKGROUND: During war, significant adaptations take place in hospitals to improve the treatment of soldiers and civilians. For example, low-risk women were discharged earlier from hospitals following delivery. The aim of the study was to compare the rate of postpartum-visits to the gynecological-emergency-room (GER) between wartime to a similar period in the previous year. METHODS: A retrospective study compared the visits of postpartum-women in the GER to a similar period in the previous year. RESULTS: The study included 801 women who delivered in the first month of the war in 2023 and 913 who delivered in the parallel period in the previous year. There were no significant changes in maternal age, gravidity, parity, mode of delivery, birthweight, meconium, low Apgar scores, and the rate of admissions to the neonatal intensive care unit. There were significantly less elective cesarean sections during wartime (57% vs. 92%; p < 0.0001). The duration of postpartum hospitalization was significantly shorter during wartime [median length of 53.2 [Interquartile-range (IQR] 42.4-72.4) hours vs. 64.1 (IQR 47.4-82.8) in the previous year (p < 0.0001)]. There were no significant differences in the rate of total referrals of postpartum-women to the GER (8.7% vs. 8.8%; p > 0.05), and no differences in referrals due to infections or bleeding. There was no difference in the rate of admission of postpartum-women (17% vs. 14%; p = 0.73). CONCLUSIONS: Shortening of hospitalization following delivery during war is feasible, does not cause increase postpartum visits to the GER, and does not increase GER visits due to infections or bleeding.

title: Fluctuations of micronutrients during pregnancy in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China: A prospective longitudinal cohort study.
abstract: Pregnancy is accompanied by substantial physiological adaptations that may alter maternal micronutrient concentrations. A prospective longitudinal pregnancy-neonatal cohort of 51 healthy pregnant women was established at 6-8 weeks of gestation in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, China, confirmed by fetal heart and bud on B-ultrasound. Pregnancy complications, outcomes, and neonatal health at day 42 were confirmed. Forty-three women who completed all assessments and had uncomplicated pregnancies with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes were included in the final analysis. Whole-blood trace elements and serum vitamins were quantified during the first trimester (12.3 ± 0.9 weeks), second trimester (25.6 ± 1.2 weeks), and third trimester (32.7 ± 2.3 weeks) using ICP-MS and UHPLC-MS/MS. The results showed that copper, calcium, and vitamin D peaked in the second trimester, whereas iron, zinc, magnesium, and lead reached their nadir in the second trimester. Meanwhile, manganese and vitamins E and K increased progressively throughout gestation. In contrast, several B vitamins showed an overall downward trend, while vitamin B12 remained relatively stable. These findings demonstrate clear trimester-specific changes in maternal micronutrient levels during healthy pregnancy. Given the relatively small sample size, these longitudinal data provide preliminary evidence to inform the establishment of region-specific and trimester-specific reference intervals and deficiency thresholds for micronutrients in healthy pregnant women.

title: Trend and factors associated with consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months in Ethiopia, Evidenced from 2005-2019 Ethiopia demographic and health survey: A multivariate decomposition analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Micro-nutrient deficiencies remain the major public health concern in sub-Saharan African countries including Ethiopia. In particular, adequate consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months in Ethiopia is very low, and is one of the reasons for the high prevalence of micronutrient deficiencies. Consumption of iron-rich food among children aged 6-23 months has changed over time in Ethiopia. However, there is scant evidence on the factors contributed for the change in the consumption of iron-rich foods. OBJECTIVE: To assess the trend and factors associated with consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months in Ethiopia based on the 2005-2019 Ethiopian Demographic Health Surveys. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A repeated cross sectional study design was employed based on the 2005, 2011, 2016 and 2019 Ethiopian Demographic Health Surveys data. A total weighted samples of 10,796 children aged 6-23 months were included. Stata version 17 statistical software was used for data management and analysis. A logit-based decomposition analysis was employed to identify factors contributing for the change in consumption of iron-rich food over time. Coefficients with the 95% Confidence Interval (CI) and P-value were reported to declare the statistical significance and strength of the contribution. RESULT: The consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months increased significantly from 10.8% (95%CI: 9.7, 11.9) in 2005 to 23.5% (95%CI:21.3, 25.6) in 2019. About 46.4% of the overall increment in the consumption of iron-rich foods among children was due to the difference in composition of women (change in endowment) across the surveys, while the difference due to the change in the effect of coefficients (change in characteristics) was insignificant. In the endowment component, the difference in composition of women with primary (23%) and secondary (10%) education, and difference in composition of women having four and above antenatal care visits (18%) were found to be significant contributing factors for the increase in the intake of iron-rich foods among young children. The increase in number of households with rich wealth status showed a 67.4% contribution for the increment of consumption of iron-rich foods during the third phase (2016-2019). CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION: Consumption of iron-rich foods among children aged 6-23 months has shown a remarkable increase over time in Ethiopia. Improvement in maternal education status, increase in number of antenatal care visits and improvement in household wealth status were the main drivers for the observed change. Strengthening policies that expand women's educational opportunities and integrate nutrition counseling into antenatal care services, and promoting household economic empowerment could further enhance iron-rich food intake. iron-rich.

title: Study on the fracture characteristics controlled by filling ratio in cut-and-fill mining.
abstract: To mitigate surface subsidence and stope instability induced by an insufficient filling ratio in cut‑and‑fill mining, this study investigates overlying strata fracture characteristics and instability mechanisms by means of similar material simulation, PFC numerical modeling, and theoretical analysis. Filling ratio acts as the dominant factor for overburden and stope stability: full (100%) filling suppresses roof displacement and key-stratum breakage to realize reliable gangue-pillar bearing and overburden control, whereas 50% insufficient filling triggers key-stratum fracture and domino-style chain failure starting from central goaf gangue pillars, further producing severe overburden destruction and large-magnitude surface subsidence. PFC simulations prove cut-and-fill mining forms a composite three-arch structure, whose evolution under gangue compaction controls overburden damage and surface subsidence. Analysis confirms the criticality of middle gangue pillar stability, so Cut-and-fill mining design should strengthen middle and end gangue pillars. This study clarifies filling ratio control mechanisms, providing technical support for filling parameter optimization and safe, efficient Cut-and-fill mining.

title: Evaluation of HPV E6/E7 mRNA in predicting recurrence after Leep in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia: A study of negative findings.
abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) is a precursor to cervical cancer, and early detection of residual or recurrent disease is therefore critical for effective management. This study evaluated whether HPV E6/E7 mRNA status predicts recurrence in patients with CIN who underwent loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). People's Hospital of Nanning between January 2019 and July 2022 were included. Patients who underwent LEEP for high-grade cervical lesions at the First Follow-up commenced 4-6 months after LEEP and continued for 24 months; abnormal findings during this period prompted referral for colposcopy or cervical biopsy. Of the 91 patients, 3 (3.30%) experienced recurrence within 24 months. Recurrence rates were similar between patients with preoperative E6/E7 mRNA positivity (3.23%) and negativity (3.45%) (p = 0.956), and between postoperative E6/E7 mRNA status groups (5.26% in the negative group vs. 0% in the positive group; p = 0.814). Although 66.7% of patients shifted from positive to negative E6/E7 mRNA status after LEEP (p < 0.001), this change was not associated with recurrence risk. Preoperative E6/E7 mRNA yielded a sensitivity of 66.67% and specificity of 31.82%, whereas postoperative E6/E7 mRNA showed a sensitivity of 0% and specificity of 97.30%. In conclusion, E6/E7 mRNA status before and after LEEP did not predict recurrence in patients with CIN. Despite a significant reduction in E6/E7 mRNA positivity after surgery, its low sensitivity underscores the need for more effective biomarkers in follow-up care.

title: Concave sparsity-assisted time-reassigned multisynchrosqueezing transform for early-stage weak fault feature enhancement with applications to bearing fault diagnosis.
abstract: Early-stage defects in wind turbine bearings often generate weak impulsive signatures that are easily obscured by strong background noise, posing a significant challenge to accurate extraction of fault-related features. To overcome this limitation, a novel concave sparsity-assisted time-reassigned multisynchrosqueezing transform (CSA-TMSST) is developed to improve the extraction of weak fault-related signatures. First, a non-convex sparse optimization model incorporating the generalized minimax-concave (GMC) penalty is established to reconstruct fault impulsive components from the raw signal. The introduced GMC-based sparse regularization enhances signal sparsity, enabling the accurate extraction of impulsive fault signatures. Subsequently, TMSST is employed to characterize the reconstructed signal in the time-frequency (TF) domain, yielding a more concentrated time-frequency representation (TFR). Furthermore, the iterative reassignment mechanism is utilized to enhance the concentration of TF energy distribution, thereby yielding a clearer TFR of transient fault features. Finally, characteristic fault frequencies are identified via spectral analysis. The results demonstrate that CSA-TMSST is capable of extracting weak fault-related signatures and producing high-quality TFRs under strong noise conditions, confirming its effectiveness and superiority.

title: Interventions with mitochondrial-related effects in older adults with type 2 diabetes: Protocol for a systematic review with conditional network meta-analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Mitochondrial dysfunction is central to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) pathogenesis, driving insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. Age-related mitochondrial impairment worsens this in older adults, yet evidence on mitochondrial interventions for this group is limited. This protocol outlines a systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating mitochondrial interventions in adults aged 60+ with T2DM. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this systematic review and conditional network meta-analysis (NMA) is to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of diverse mitochondrial-related interventions, including pharmacological agents, nutritional supplements, and lifestyle modifications, relative to placebo, standard care, or no intervention, on mitochondrial function biomarkers in adults aged 60 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Interventions with mitochondrial effects are operationally defined as those whose primary mechanism is known to target mitochondrial pathways or those that are explicitly evaluated for their effects on direct markers of mitochondrial function in the trial. The secondary objectives are: (1) to assess the impact of these interventions on glycemic and metabolic control outcomes including glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting insulin, homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), body weight, and body mass index (BMI); (2) to conduct a conditional NMA to compare and rank the relative efficacy of different intervention categories if the evidence network is sufficiently connected and clinically coherent; and (3) to explore potential sources of heterogeneity (e.g., intervention duration, baseline HbA1c levels) via prespecified subgroup and sensitivity analyses. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prepared per PRISMA-P, the review will follow PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA if applicable. Registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420251145356), searches will cover PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus from inception to April 2026. Focused on T2DM, mitochondrial function/dysfunction, and interventions, age eligibility will be assessed during full-text screening. Primary analysis includes trials with participants aged 60+ or extractable data for this group; sensitivity analyses will include those with mean/median age ≥ 60. Two reviewers will handle screening, data extraction, and bias assessment using RoB 2.Analysis will focus on trials reporting mitochondrial function outcomes, categorized by biological domain, tissue source, and assay method. Glycemic control, geriatric health, and safety are secondary outcomes. Network meta-analysis will be conducted if a connected evidence network exists; otherwise, pairwise meta-analysis or narrative synthesis will be used. Random-effects models will be employed, with heterogeneity assessed via subgroup analysis and meta-regression. If significant heterogeneity persists, a Synthesis Without Meta-Analysis (SWiM) framework narrative review will be done. Evidence certainty will be appraised using GRADE and CINeMA. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: Ethics approval is not required for this systematic review as the systematic review will include only previously anonymised data from primary studies. Dissemination of the findings of the final systematic review will occur through publishing in a peer-reviewed journal. PROSPERO registration number CRD420251145356.

title: Concurrent TMS-EEG to characterise interhemispheric signal propagation over the motor and prefrontal regions: An independent replication of GABAB receptor mechanisms.
abstract: Callosal abnormalities disrupt interhemispheric communications that impair the recovery of a series of neurological and psychiatric disorders. Understanding interhemispheric communication could help identify treatments for disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission. This study aimed to validate the sensitivity of a TMS-EEG-based measure of interhemispheric signal propagation (ISP) to GABAB receptor modulation, while independently replicating the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition. A group of 29 participants received an oral dose of either baclofen, a GABAB receptor agonist, or a placebo. Before and after drug intake, single-pulse TMS-EEG was applied to assess ISP in both the motor and prefrontal regions. Our findings indicated that baclofen increased interhemispheric inhibition over the motor region, indexed by significantly decreased ISP (p = 0.037). No significant effect was observed in the dorsolateral prefrontal region (p = 0.186), suggesting regional specificity in GABAB receptor modulation of ISP. These findings uncovered the pharmacological mechanisms of interhemispheric inhibition as indexed by ISP. They also highlight the potential of ISP for characterising interhemispheric communication, which could inform the treatment for a series of disorders with dysfunctional callosal transmission.

title: Design and verification of an interlocked centrifugal exhaust system for hatch-type boiling disinfectors.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To address the occupational exposure risks caused by instantaneous steam overflow when opening the top cover of hatch-type boiling disinfectors in the central sterile supply department, this study developed an interlocked centrifugal exhaust system (ICES) characterized by operational simplicity and high adaptability. METHODS: The ICES was assembled using a centrifugal fan, Hall effect switch, instant relay, time-delay relay, solid-state relay, and piping. The system achieved automatic start/stop of the fan based on the open‑or‑closed status of the top cover. A self-controlled design was adopted on one hatch-type boiling disinfector. Temperature was measured at the chamber edge (T1) and at the technician's facial position (T2). Airborne particle counts were also measured at the technician's facial position. Measurements were performed under conditions with and without the ICES enabled. Data were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. RESULTS: After enabling the ICES, T1 and T2 decreased by 20.89% and 31.31%, respectively. The median temperature at T2 was 21.5 °C, which was close to the ambient temperature. The reduction ratios for airborne particle counts of six different sizes at the technician's facial position ranged from 53.09% to 67.83%. All differences between groups were statistically significant (all P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The ICES effectively reduces steam overflow upon the top-cover opening of hatch-type boiling disinfectors and lowers the risk of occupational injury. With advantages such as wide installation adaptability, imperceptible operation, and convenient maintenance, it provides a stable and reliable solution for the safety retrofitting of existing hatch-type boiling disinfectors.

title: Retrospective analysis of genetic diversity, clinical manifestations and risk factors, during outbreak of lumpy skin disease virus.
abstract: Lumpy skin is a highly host-specific, contagious, transboundary, notifiable disease affecting cattle (Bos taurus and Bos indicus) and water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis), and also reported in some wild ruminants. The spread and reporting of Lumpy skin disease (LSD) in the past five years in disease-free countries, mainly in Pakistan, has highlighted the threat of its emergence and re-emergence in neighboring areas. Notably significant outbreaks of this disease have been reported in the neighboring countries of Pakistan during the last decades and are thought to be the reason for the first reported outbreak of LSD in Pakistan in the year 2021-22. This study targeted seven locations and collected samples and clinical data of LSD-suspected animals, focusing on clinical presentation, farm-level risk factors, and molecular characterization via PCR and subsequent phylogenetic relatedness of sequenced isolates. Out of the collected samples (n = 285), 117 cases were found positive for LSDV. The most frequent clinical signs included fever (83.7%), skin nodules (94.8%), emaciation (88.0%), and snoring (83.7%), all of which were statistically significant (p ≤ 0.05). Significant farm-level risk factors associated with LSDV positive cases included the use of shared water sources (64.9%), treatment by quack practitioners (79.4%), improper handling of manure (22.2%), and lack of disinfection (15.3%), with significant p-values ≤0.05. Molecular confirmation of LSDV was performed by PCR amplification of a 554-bp fragment of the RPO30 gene, a commonly used molecular marker for LSDV detection and characterization. The sequenced isolates showed close genetic similarity to strains reported from India, Bangladesh, and China, indicating a regional genetic relatedness among circulating LSDV strains. The study highlights that enhanced biosecurity, farmer education, vaccination, and veterinary guidance can prevent disease spread, improve livestock health, and reduce economic losses.

title: Non-monotonic thickness dependence of MoS2-Sb contact resistance driven by bandgap and interlayer transport.
abstract: Contact resistance at metal-two-dimensional semiconductor interfaces is a major factor limiting the performance of emerging two-dimensional electronic devices. Understanding how material thickness influences contact behavior is therefore essential for device optimization. Here, we systematically investigate the layer-dependent contact resistance of MoS2-Sb interfaces using MoS2 field-effect transistors with different layer numbers. Contact resistance was extracted using the transmission line method and compared for devices fabricated on SiO2 and HfO2 gate dielectrics. The results reveal a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of contact resistance on the MoS2 layer number. As the layer number increases from one to three, the contact resistance decreases and reaches a minimum value of 308 Ω·μm for trilayer MoS2, while further increasing the thickness leads to a rise in resistance. Analysis of the electronic band structure and interlayer transport mechanisms indicates that this behavior originates from the competition between bandgap reduction and increasing interlayer transport resistance. In the few-layer regime, bandgap narrowing lowers the Schottky barrier and reduces contact resistance, whereas in thicker layers the growing interlayer resistance dominates carrier transport. These findings provide important insight into thickness-dependent contact physics in two-dimensional semiconductors and offer practical guidance for optimizing contact engineering and channel thickness in next-generation electronic devices.

title: Improved vision transformer for sports image classification via transfer learning and knowledge distillation.
abstract: To address the challenges posed by complex visual characteristics in sports image classification, this study proposes an enhanced Vision Transformer (ViT) model built upon the Native Resolution ViT (NaViT) architecture. The principal innovations include replacing conventional single-layer feedforward networks with parallel feedforward networks and introducing an attention-guided distillation framework with input-dependent attention-weighted feature fusion, which adaptively regulates the contribution of frozen distillation features to the prediction pathway. The proposed approach leverages ImageNet-pretrained weights and performs domain-specific fine-tuning on sports datasets. Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains. On the multi-sport classification dataset, the proposed model achieves an accuracy of 0.9752 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9753, outperforming the evaluated CNN benchmarks and ViT variants. For soccer match event classification, it achieves an accuracy of 0.9863 and a Macro-F1 score of 0.9718, while ranking first in the TOPSIS evaluation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating parallel feedforward processing, transfer learning, and distillation-guided feature fusion for sports image classification under complex visual conditions.

title: Multidimensional oral health and frailty in older adults: A sex-stratified cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty in older adults is a critical public health concern associated with increased morbidity, disability, and healthcare utilization. Although systemic health and socioeconomic factors are well-established determinants of frailty, the multidimensional nature of oral health has received relatively limited attention in previous research. The aim of this study was to examine the associations between general characteristics, health-related factors, oral health factors, and frailty among community-dwelling older adults, and to identify sex differences in frailty. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2022 Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging (KLoSA) and included 3,729 individuals aged 65 years and older. Frailty was categorized as robust, pre-frail, or frail using the Frailty Instrument developed for older Korean adults. General characteristics, health-related factors, and oral health-related factors (structural, behavioral, and subjective) were assessed through structured questionnaires. Hierarchical logistic regression analysis was performed in three steps to identify factors associated with frailty. RESULTS: Of the participants, 16.0% were frail and 84.0% were non-frail (31.5% pre-frail and 52.5% robust). Sex-stratified analyses also showed that structural oral health factors were most strongly associated with frailty in both sexes. Edentulous status without denture use was associated with the highest odds of frailty in both women (OR = 3.76, 95% CI = 3.72-3.80) and men (OR = 2.95, 95% CI = 2.91-2.98). In contrast, sex differences were observed for some subjective oral health factors: tooth sensitivity was associated with higher odds of frailty in women (OR = 1.82, 95% CI = 1.80-1.84) but lower odds in men (OR = 0.85, 95% CI = 0.84-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: Oral health conditions, including untreated tooth loss, difficulty in chewing or swallowing, and oral pain, were significantly associated with frailty. These findings suggest that oral health may be an important factor to consider in relation to frailty among community-dwelling older adults.

Linguistic Context Shapes Representations in the Human Visual Cortex
abstract: Language provides a way to anticipate visual scenes before they are seen, but how this context relates to visual representations across levels of abstraction remains unclear. Here, 210 hours of functional magnetic resonance imaging from eight participants performing a delayed caption-image matching task are analyzed using computational encoding, decoding, and alignment models. Caption-evoked activity carries semantic information across visual cortex, including early visual areas. Subsequent image responses vary with both the strength of caption-derived contextual representations and the discrepancy between anticipated and viewed scenes, assessed across lower-level visual and higher-level semantic features. Two functionally distinct voxel populations are identified within early visual cortex: suppression populations respond less strongly to matching than mismatching images, whereas enhancement populations show the opposite pattern. Despite their lower responses to matching images, suppression populations support comparable or better retrieval of corresponding caption-evoked responses using fewer voxels. The two populations also differ in their temporal dynamics, representational structure, and relationship to behavior. Together, these findings link linguistic context to both the strength and informational content of visual cortical responses, revealing how language-vision relationships are expressed across representational levels and two functionally distinct populations in early visual cortex.

title: Directional coordination along the cortical hierarchy is selectively reorganized in schizophrenia
abstract: Schizophrenia has long been framed as a disorder of the cortical hierarchy. Yet, the hierarchy has been studied almost entirely as fixed anatomy, leaving its moment-to-moment expression in ongoing brain activity unmeasured. By retaining the signed lead-lag geometry that conventional connectivity measures discard, complex-valued phase synchrony resolved a dynamic directional axis of coordination in which regions reversed their lead-lag relationship over time as the brain transitioned among feedback, feedforward, and integrative regimes. The three regimes replicated across seven datasets from four independent cohorts and aligned region by region with an independently defined cortical hierarchy. Neighboring organizing principles, including propagating waves, arousal, and the principal gradient, were insufficient to explain regime identity. Within the same subjects, GABAergic sedation shifted coordination toward feedback and motor imagery toward feedforward, demonstrating that the axis reflects a manipulable property of brain dynamics rather than a statistical partition. In schizophrenia (151 patients, 160 controls), the axis reorganized selectively: feedback coordination became less persistent, integrative coordination more persistent, feedforward comparatively spared, and trajectories less diverse. These effects replicated in an independent clinical cohort (68 patients, 89 controls). The reorganization tracked positive symptom severity, and its relationship to cognition reversed relative to controls: faster convergence to equilibrium was associated with better cognition in controls and worse cognition in patients. Directional coordination therefore identifies a reproducible and controllable dynamic expression of the cortical hierarchy that is selectively reorganized in schizophrenia and linked to both symptoms and cognitive function.

title: Decoupling of spontaneous and evoked activity in locus coeruleus neurons: early synaptic and ion-channel remodeling in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease
abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) is among the earliest brain regions affected in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the mechanisms underlying its early vulnerability remain poorly understood. Clarifying synaptic and intrinsic dysfunction in LC noradrenergic (NE) neurons is essential to determine how noradrenergic circuit failure contributes to prodromal AD. We combined whole-cell patch-clamp recordings with quantitative immunofluorescence to examine synaptic transmission, firing properties, voltage-gated currents, and synaptic organization in LC/NE neurons from young 3xTg mice prior to substantial neurodegeneration. Young 3xTg mice exhibited reduced excitatory and enhanced inhibitory synaptic input onto LC/NE neurons. Consistent with these functional shifts, structural analysis revealed decreased densities of VGLUT2, PSD95, and paired VGLUT2-PSD95 puncta, alongside increased VGAT, gephyrin, and paired VGAT-gephyrin puncta. Despite this net synaptic suppression, LC/NE neurons displayed elevated spontaneous firing rates but a markedly reduced capacity to generate spike output during sustained depolarization. Voltage-clamp recordings revealed a diminished total voltage-gated K current density alongside reduced voltage-gated Na current density, without significant shifts in their voltage-dependence or kinetics. These biophysical alterations provide a mechanistic basis for the divergent firing phenotype: reduced K current; conductance likely facilitates spontaneous pacemaker activity, whereas diminished Na current; current constrains repetitive, input-driven spike generation. Together, these findings demonstrate that LC/NE neurons undergo coordinated synaptic and ion-channel remodeling during prodromal AD. This unique decoupling of spontaneous baseline activity from stimulus-evoked excitability may impair dynamic noradrenergic modulation, positioning early LC cellular dysfunction as a candidate driver of network instability and a novel therapeutic target.

title: Dynamics of dopamine transients in human olfactory epithelium during reward learning
abstract: Dopamine signaling is crucial for motivation, movement, and learning, but has remained beyond the reach of measurement in healthy humans. Here, we measured sub-second dopamine in the olfactory epithelium of healthy humans during two reward learning tasks with distinct reward types: liquid reward during a conditioning task and monetary reward during an economic exchange game. In both tasks, as trials progress, peak dopamine transients shift from rewarding outcomes back to reward-predictive cues. In the economic game, this pattern retrains quickly when reward magnitude or reward timing is changed without warning. These findings match the time transfer characteristics and amplitude dependence of temporal difference prediction error signals. The results also establish a new, minimally invasive route for recording fast dopamine signaling in healthy humans: the nose.
author_corresponding_institution: Fralin Biomedical Research Institute at Virginia Tech

title: Variabilities in the shapes of the receptive fields of simple cells in mice
abstract: Observing an object under different viewing conditions, in spite of substantial variability in the image structures when changing the distance or the viewing direction relative to the object, we can maintain the identity of the object. How does the vision system cope with this variability, that will substantially influence the receptive field responses? One hypothesis is that the receptive field family should be covariant under geometric image transformations and thereby have variabilities in the shapes of the receptive fields corresponding to the degrees of freedom of the geometric image transformations. Specifically, it has been predicted that the receptive fields should have a variability in the degree of elongation, corresponding to varying the slant angle when observing local surface patches. Such a variability has also been predicted from indirect support in terms of variabilities in the orientation selectivity properties in V1 for monkeys and cats, which by a theoretical model has been linked to variabilities in the elongation of th receptive fields. In this paper, we measure such variabilities in receptive field shapes in a more direct way, by reconstructing receptive fields from calcium imaging experiments for mice previously performed by the Allen Institute. Our findings reveal a variability in the degree of elongation that exceeds what measurement noise produces, spanning about a factor of 5, thereby showing that the predictions that were made for higher mammals with orientation maps, such as primates and cats, also apply to a species without orientation maps, with its primary visual cortex instead based on a salt-and-pepper organization of the receptive fields.

title: Cortex-wide single-cell activity mapping in freely moving mice
abstract: How the cortex supports complex, naturalistic behavior can be revealed only in freely moving animals. Although head-mounted microscopes promise access to the neural dynamics underlying such behavior, fundamental trade-offs among field of view, spatial resolution, device weight, and background contamination have prevented cortex-wide single-neuron recording, leaving distributed cortical coordination largely inaccessible. To meet these challenges, we introduce COMET (Cortex-wide Observational Miniature Epifluorescence Technique), a 3.75-g head-mounted mesoscope that integrates an aberration-controlled wide-field optical design, uniform high-efficiency excitation and single-coaxial power-and-data transmission with an end-to-end denoising and signal-extraction pipeline. This enables cortex-wide calcium imaging at single-cell resolution in freely moving mice. COMET captures activity from >15,000 layer 2/3 neurons per 5-min recording over fields of view up to 10 mm in diameter while preserving natural behavior. Benchmarking against benchtop two-photon microscopy demonstrates high spatial concordance of detected neurons and matched event-level calcium dynamics. We apply COMET to social interaction to quantify region-specific engagement and to an auditory trace fear-conditioning task that requires natural movement and behavioral expression, revealing time-ordered changes in regional firing-rate structure and functional connectivity preceding a global conditioned response. COMET provides an open, lightweight hardware-software framework for linking single-neuron activity to cortex-scale network dynamics during freely expressed behaviors under changing internal or external conditions.

title: Aging effects on retrospective and naturalistic encoding of time and their relationship with memory.
abstract: In everyday life, attention is not explicitly directed toward time. Yet, we can reconstruct how long an experience lasted from the memory traces it left behind, a process intertwined with episodic memory and subjective experience. As both memory and temporal processing change with advancing age, investigating aging effects could provide critical insights on these reconstructive processes. In this study, 31 younger (aged 24{+/-}3) and 36 older (aged 69{+/-}6) healthy adults completed two EEG sessions: 1) a resting-state recording followed by an unexpected retrospective time estimation, and 2) a video-based prospective duration estimation task where participants encoded and judged the duration of 50 naturalistic videos (2-32s) varying in eventfulness. Using a cycle-by-cycle burst analysis of alpha (: 8-12 Hz), we examined oscillatory correlates of both retrospective temporal judgement and prospective temporal processing. Behaviorally, both groups reconstructed short intervals similarly, but older adults produced longer prospective duration estimates than younger adults for longer video clips (16-32s), particularly under low-eventfulness. Regression analyses also showed that individual differences in older adults' prospective duration judgments were influenced by both their retrospective time estimation and episodic memory abilities, especially for longer videos. At the neural level, resting-state -burst dynamics were higher in older adults and predicted, with -power, longer retrospective estimates in older adults. Additionally, resting-state -burst activity predicted -burst during video encoding in both groups. Together, these findings reveal that individual -power and -burst dynamics could constitute memory-based time-tracking mechanism that aging reshapes in ways that manifest behaviorally under naturalistic conditions.

title: Grasping Under Target Size and Location Uncertainty
abstract: Everyday actions often require movements to be planned before the exact target is known, yet most research on grasping has examined situations in which individuals reach toward a single, well-defined object. The present study investigated how grasping actions are planned under target uncertainty using a go-before-you-know (GBYK) paradigm, in which participants initiated their movement before knowing which of two potential objects would become the target. Using 3D motion capture, we examined whether peak grip aperture (PGA) was influenced by the size of a competing nontarget object. Participants grasped cylindrical objects that varied in size under two conditions: GBYK, in which target identity was revealed after movement initiation, and know-before-you-go (KBYG), in which the target was known prior to movement onset. Across two experiments, participants appropriately scaled grip aperture according to the target object in both conditions. However, during GBYK trials, PGA was influenced by the presence of a larger nontarget object. Specifically, when grasping a small target paired with a large nontarget, participants produced larger grip apertures, whereas a small nontarget did not influence grasping toward a large target. This asymmetric interference pattern is inconsistent with a motor averaging account, which predicts bidirectional shifts toward an intermediate aperture. Instead, the findings suggest that under conditions of uncertainty, grasp planning incorporates competing object information in a manner that prioritizes successful object acquisition. Together, these findings extend research on action planning under uncertainty beyond reaching and highlight the dynamic nature of grasp planning when multiple potential targets are present.

title: Movie Watching for Individual Functional Brain Network Estimation in Adolescents
abstract: Precision functional mapping (PFM) reveals stable individual differences in brain functional network organization and holds promise for advancing neuropsychiatric clinical care. PFM requires sufficient high-quality and densely-sampled functional MRI data at the individual level that is typically acquired during the so-called resting state while passively fixating on a crosshair. However, crosshair fixation acquisitions can be challenging especially for pediatric or patient populations, where alternatives like movie watching might be used to improve data quality and reduce participant burden. Here, we compare the use of resting state crosshair fixation and movie watching fMRI data to derive individual-specific functional brain network topography using PFM data (28-38 minutes of low-motion fMRI data per-participant per-condition) in nineteen adolescents (12-18 years) with a range of transdiagnostic psychiatric diagnoses. Network assignments were largely conserved between crosshair fixation and movie watching, with a smaller subset of reproducible network reassignments which were overwhelmingly border shifts between neighboring networks. This suggests largely conserved global structure of functional network topography between crosshair fixation and movie watching, though border shifts can compound into variable estimates of cortical network size particularly for movie positive (language, salience, and parietal memory) and movie negative networks (default mode, action mode). Functional network assignments derived from movies and crosshair were also similarly individual-specific and consistent within common neuromodulation targets including dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and somatomotor cortex. Key results were replicated in independent pediatric consortia data (Healthy Brain Network, n = 466, 6-22 years) and reproduced across independent PFM data sessions. Acknowledging individual differences and level of analysis, we conclude that movies are a viable alternative to resting state crosshair fixation for individual network definitions.

title: The vagus nerve drives cognitive function through the default mode network
abstract: The afferent vagus nerve transmits interoceptive signals to the brain but a systematic understanding of how vagal signals affect brain-wide neuronal dynamics remains elusive. Here, comprehensive spatiotemporal analyses across the entire mouse brain revealed that vagus nerve stimulation activated neuronal ensembles within the default mode network (DMN). In contrast, vagal-independent mechanisms predominantly affected the salience network. The vagal-DMN association was mediated by locus coeruleus neuronal subpopulations. Selective activation or silencing of vagal-responsive DMN neuronal ensembles replicated or abolished VNS-induced enhancement of cognitive behaviors and progressive problem-solving behaviors. These findings establish a unifying framework for how the vagus nerve drives cognitive functions by engaging the DMN.

title: Dishevelled2 Condensates control Axon Initial Segment (AIS) assembly and function through MTCL1-Dependent microtubule recruitment.
abstract: In the epithelium, Planar Cell Polarity (PCP) signaling coordinates cellular organization along the plane of the tissue, perpendicular to the apicobasal axis. In neurons, polarity is instead expressed through the structural and molecular asymmetry that separates the axon from the somatodendritic compartment. Core PCP proteins are essential for neuronal development and function, and have been linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, including autism spectrum disorders and epilepsy. However, their precise roles in the establishment of neuronal polarity remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify Dishevelled2 (Dvl2), a central PCP signaling scaffold, as a novel component of the axon initial segment (AIS), the proximal axonal domain that maintains neuronal polarity and initiates action potentials. We show that Dvl2 defines, both in vivo and in cultured hippocampal neurons, a proximal subdomain positioned upstream of the major AIS marker Ankyrin-G (Ank-G) and is closely associated with microtubule bundles. Dvl2 is already detected during early axon specification, suggesting that it participates in the initial organization of the proximal axon. Functional depletion of Dvl proteins disrupts AIS architecture, reduces the accumulation of Ankyrin-G and other core AIS components, and impairs the organization of AIS microtubule bundles. These structural defects translate into altered neuronal excitability, with a reduced AIS-dependent component of the action potential. Mechanistically, we identify MTCL1 as a microtubule-associated partner that recruits Dvl2 from biomolecular condensate assemblies onto microtubules. This recruitment requires the DIX and PDZ domains of Dvl2. Notably, selective intracellular binders targeting the Dvl2 PDZ domain perturb Dvl2 condensate organization and compromise AIS formation. Together, our data identify Dvl2 as an organizer of the proximal AIS and reveal a Dvl2-MTCL1-dependent mechanism coupling condensate scaffolding, microtubule organization, and neuronal excitability.

title: A novel behavioral paradigm to model hypermemory-like features in rats
abstract: Episodic memory is essential to everyday life and personal identity. However, its dysfunctions can profoundly affect mental health, and translational methods for investigating them in animals remain limited. Most rodent paradigms focus on memory deficits, whereas few tools model abnormally enhanced and persistent memories. Here, we developed a behavioral paradigm to induce hypermemory-like features in adult male and female rats using a version of object recognition (OR) and object location (OL) tasks specifically modified to mimic the rumination-like component of hypermemory. During the odor-context association training, rats explored two identical objects in the presence of a cinnamon scent. Over the following 6 h, they received 12 brief re-exposures in their home cage to either the cinnamon odor or an odor-free stimulus. By repeatedly reactivating the memory trace, these re-exposures promoted its hyperconsolidation without re-exposing animals to the original context or objects. Twenty-four hours later, memory was assessed under odor-free conditions. Odor re-exposure selectively enhanced OL memory in rats of both sexes, whereas OR memory remained unaffected. The procedure did not alter total object exploration or locomotor activity. Enhanced spatial memory was also accompanied by increased c-Fos expression in the ventral hippocampus in both sexes. Our protocol recapitulates key features observed in individuals with hyperfunctional episodic memory: continuous memory reactivation and rumination which may contribute to the excessive strengthening and persistence of specific memories. This simple and reproducible paradigm provides a novel translational tool for investigating the behavioral and neurobiological mechanisms underlying memory hyperconsolidation and maladaptive memory persistence.

title: Parathyroid Hormone Receptor 1 Signaling Encodes Multifaceted Metabolic Programs in AgRP Neurons
abstract: Organisms continuously adapt food intake and nutrient utilization to fluctuating energy demands, requiring the brain to accurately integrate signals coming from diverse metabolic organs and local signals into distinct physiological responses. How hypothalamic neurons discriminate these signals to independently regulate feeding behavior and peripheral metabolism remains poorly understood. In recent years, a coordinated regulation between bone physiology and the central control of energy metabolism has emerged, opening questions about potential common hormonal networks and signaling pathways between the bone and the brain. Here, we identify parathyroid hormone receptor 1 (PTH1R) signaling, a master regulator of calcium ion biochemistry and bone formation, in Agouti-related peptide (AgRP) neurons as an unexpected neuroendocrine mechanism for the control of feeding behaviourand nutrient partitioning. the two cognate endocrine and paracrine ligands, PTH and PTH-related peptide (PTHrP), selectively activat segregated intracellular kinases activation and lipophagic processes in AgRP neuron, ultimately producing convergent physiological outputs. Together, our findings identify the parathyroid hormonal system acts as a fine-tuning mechanism in specialized neuronal circuits allowing for hypothalamic adaptive responses to energy demands and systemic metabolic signals. Keywords: Parathyroid hormone-related peptide (PTHrP), hypothalamus, arcuate nucleus, agouti-related peptide neurons, energy metabolism, fasting, autophagy, free fatty acids
author_corresponding_institution: Universite Paris Cite, CNRS, Unite de Biologie Fonctionnelle et Adaptative

title: Autoencoder-based anomaly mapping and visualization of white matter deformation with application to glioma cases
abstract: Introduction: Gliomas can alter white matter pathways, causing structural deformation and functional impairments. However, there is no method to map these structural alterations across the whole brain to support diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. To address this gap, we propose a novel framework based on a convolutional autoencoder that learns geometry-preserving streamline embeddings for mapping structural connectivity anomalies. Methods: We trained and validated the autoencoder on 100 million synthetic streamlines and evaluated the anomaly-mapping pipeline using data from 118 healthy subjects. We analyzed how different tractography algorithms affect anomaly scores and demonstrated its feasibility in five glioma patients using multi-shell and single-shell diffusion MRI. Results: Latent-space distances strongly associated with native-space geometric distances (R2 = 0.82-0.98), supporting preserved streamline geometry in the learned embeddings. Anomaly scores varied with both the input and reference tractography methods. Patient anomaly maps showed elevated scores near gliomas and extending distally along affected pathways. These whole-brain anomaly maps were generated within minutes. Conclusion: The framework offers a practical way to quantify and visualize geometric deviations in whole-brain tractograms, providing novel insights beyond current network and microstructural analyses, with relevance to clinical applications where white matter deformation is pertinent.
author_corresponding_institution: A.I. Virtanen Institute for Molecular Sciences, University of Eastern Finland, Kuopio

title: Agency and Embodiment Provide Dissociable Benefits to Perception, Metacognition and Neural Processing During Active Sensing
abstract: Metacognition, judging how reliable our own perceptual decisions are, is central to adaptive behavior. Such judgments hinge on the reliability of the sensory evidence on which that decision is based, and active sensing through self-directed exploration is known to improve perception itself. Yet, how agency, the authorship over self-initiated actions, and the processing of the sensory consequences, which is implicit to active sensing, modulate metacognition and its calibration, remains unknown. Whether physical embodiment adds to this beyond virtual exploration is similarly unclear, yet relevant both for daily life and for self-monitoring in agentic AI. Here, we combined a naturalistic auditory search paradigm with mobile electroencephalography. Twenty participants performed a target-detection task under three conditions: active embodied exploration , active screen-based exploration, and passive listening to replays of their own trials, while we obtained steady-state auditory evoked potentials (SSAEPs) to characterize stimulus-locked neural responses. We find that both agency conditions improved accuracy, metacognitive sensitivity, and overall SSAEP amplitude relative to passive listening, indicating that agency, rather than whole-body movement, drives these enhancements. Crucially, however, embodiment uniquely grounded both the target-evoked neural response and the subjects' confidence to immediate sensory evidence. Thus, agency alone broadly enhances perceptual and neural processing, but embodiment specifically anchors confidence, neurally and behaviorally, to the present.
